name: Computer Architecture and Operating Systems
text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
Computer Architecture and Operating Systems  
(Архитектура компьютера и операционные системы) 
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Informatics and Computational 
Experiment E.M. Andreeva 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
The complexity of the discipline is 5 credit units (180 hours), of which 54 hours of lectures, 
36 hours of laboratory studies, 54 hours for independent work, 36 hours for exam preparation. 
Reporting form - exam. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Computer Architecture and Operating Systems (Архитектура 
компьютера и операционные системы) ” (3 course, 5 semester) refers to the basic part of the 
discipline block. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by the 
previous disciplines “ Basics of Programming (Основы программирования) " , "Discrete 
Mathematics (Дискретная математика) " , "Programming Languages (Языки 
программирования)". 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to 
solve professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, 
in the development of algorithms and programs as part of the preparation of the final 
qualification work. 
4. Objectives of studying the discipline 
purpose mastering the discipline - studying the principles of construction and architecture 
of modern computers and operating systems (OS).  
Tasks: 
• Acquaintance with the main stages of the historical development of computer technology.  
• Study of the role of each of the main components of a computing system in its 
organization.  
• Familiarity with the principles of microprogram control.  
• The study of ways to represent numbers in the memory of computers, the level of the 
instruction set.  
• Acquaintance with basic instructions from the x86 set, programming in assembly 
language. 
• Acquaintance with the purpose, history of development of the OS, with the general 
organization of the OS. 
• Acquaintance with the concept of asynchronous processes, methods of organizing their 
interaction, methods of implementing processes and distributing processor time between 
processes. 
• Acquaintance with memory management methods, resource protection methods, features 
of the OS design and debugging process, formal models of parallel processes. 
• the acquisition of skills in the development of individual OS subsystems and the 
organization of program execution in the environment of modern OS. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, 
skills and abilities: 
To understand and analyze: 
• the main stages in the development of computing technology, methods of classifying 
computers, 
• the constituent parts of a computing system and the problems of their development 
and interaction, 
• levels of computer architecture, their purpose and interaction, 
• basic digital logic circuits and buses used in computers, 
• problems of microprogram control of the central processor, 
• tasks solved by the instruction set level, 
• ways of representing numbers in a computer, 
• x86 instruction set kernels. 
• concepts of asynchronous processes, methods of implementing processes, means of 
synchronizing processes, deadlock problems and methods for their detection; 
• methods of allocating processor time; 
• methods for managing RAM and implementing virtual memory, methods for 
managing external devices, methods for implementing file systems; 
• main methods of protecting resources in the OS, features of the design and 
debugging of the OS, formal models of parallel processes. 
To create and to be able to: 
• solve standard problems of developing projects of OS components, taking into 
account the basic requirements of information security. 
• determine the type of computing architecture,  
• define the representation of numbers in machines with different RAM organization,  
• use the simplest error-correcting codes: parity checks, (7,4) -Hamming,  
• predict the behavior of the simplest digital logic circuits,  
• compose fragments of microprogram for the simplest microarchitectures,  
• to compose programs in assembly language for the processor of the x86 family. 
To apply: 
• development and debugging of programs in the environment of modern operating 
systems, 
• development and debugging of programs in assembly language.  
 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following 
competencies: 
 General professional competences (ОПК) 
 ОПК -5. Able to install and maintain software for information systems and databases, including 
those of domestic origin, taking into account information security 
 Indicator 
 ОПК -5.1. Installs information systems and databases 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Computer architecture 
The concepts of architecture and organization of the computer. The development of computer 
technology. A variety of computers, Moore's law. 
Overview of the central processor. Logical equivalence of hardware and software, the principle 
of microprogram control. 
Design of modern processors, CISC and RISC. Parallel computing systems 
Memory hierarchy. Random access memory, RAM organization issues: cells, byte order. Cache 
memory: cache memory. 
Secondary memory, magnetic disk device, CHS geometry, primary interfaces. Anti -jamming 
coding. I / O subsystem, system buses, chipset. 
Digital logic level. Transistors, gates, logic circuits, printed circuit boards. Combinational 
circuits, sequential circuits (memory circuits), clock generators. 
System bus design issues: width, skew, multiplexing, arbitration, (a) synchronicity. Serial and 
parallel buses. 
Microarchitecture level. Data path, internal registers, organization of the control device in the 
form of microprogram. An example of the Mic -1 microarchitecture and the implementation of 
the simplest IJVM instructions using it 
Instruction set level design issues. Representation of numeric data types: signed integers, floating 
point numbers 
 
Section 2. Operating Systems  
Basic OS concepts. The evolution of operating systems, the emergence of modern operating 
systems. OS classification by architecture. System call interface. Kernel data structures. 
Multitasking and process concept. OS functions for process control. Multi -state process models, 
examples. Process table and control block: purpose and content. Creation, switching and 
termination of OS processes. The relationship between the concepts of process and flow. 
Multithreading implementation schemes. Operations on streams. 
Classification of processes by behavior. Planning problems, categories of planning algorithms. 
Examples of algorithms. Three -tier planning. Planning in interactive systems. Features of 
scheduling flows. 
The concepts of race condition and mutual exclusion. Software and hardware approaches to the 
implementation of mutual exclusion. Variants of Decker's algorithm, Peterson's algorithm. 
Synchronization primitives: mutual exclusion using semaphores, conditional variables, Hoare 
monitors. Read / write locks, barrier synchronization, message passing. 
Memory management subsystem functions. Process address space. Memory allocation methods. 
Address translation problem. Paging and Segment Memory Organization 
Benefits of using technology. The problem of address translation, options for implementing page 
tables. Fast Transform Buffer (TLB), cache. Virtual memory for paging, segment and combined 
organization. Virtual memory management algorithms. 
Strategies for evading and swapping pages and virtual memory segments. Memory management 
in UNIX OS. 
Categories of I / O devices. Software and hardware support for I / O: evolution of I / O methods, 
programmable, using interrupts, with direct memory access. Device independent software. 
Device drivers. 
Physical device of the hard disk, addressing, reading order. Partitioning a hard disk, examples of 
partitioning for specific OS. OS boot order. File concept, content, attributes, formats. File access 
methods. Files in processes. File directories: operations, structure, use. Hard and soft links. 
Access rights. Mount file systems. 
File system area of responsibility. Block sizes. File allocation methods: continuous, linked lists, 
allocation tables, index nodes. Placement of directories, examples of some OS. Accounting for 
free blocks. File system quotas. Archiving. Productivity issues. 
Deadlock concept, occurrence examples. Formal definition, conditions for the occurrence of 
deadlocks. Control strategies. Simulation of deadlocks. Eliminate deadlock conditions. Detection 
and recovery algorithms. Prevention methods, safe states, banker's algorithm. 
Basic concepts, components of a computer system. Computer security tasks, threat classification. 
Types of malware. Defense mechanisms. Types of authentication. Security domains, access 
control lists, feature lists. Intrusion detection, basic techniques. System audit, virus protection. 
Features of the process of designing and debugging the OS. Hardware support for OS 
implementation in Intel processors in its virtual (protected) mode of operation. Segment and 
paging memory organization. Process switching support. Mutual protection of processes. 
Formal models of parallel processes. Petri nets, computational schemes. Graph models for 
working with shared resources. 
Hoare's model of interacting sequential processes. Recursive definition of processes, protocols of 
processes, model of the problem of five dining philosophers. 
The Five Dinner Philosophers Problem Model: Proof of the Presence and Absence of Deadlocks 
for Different Problem Solving Options 
Questions for self-study 
Implementation of various approaches and theoretical aspects of OS organization in UNIX -like 
versions of operating systems. Sections of the theory on the topics of individual assignments. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies are 
used: 
● multimedia lectures; 
● electronic forms of control; 
● testing of graduates; 
● self-test of students 
● individual control. 
The educational process is focused on the formation of a specific list of professional 
competencies, updating the obtained theoretical knowledge. Innovative methods of organizing 
the educational process are used, including technologies of guided self -study, including, in 
particular, the use of a point -rating system, as well as the introduction of an online support 
system for students' out-of-class work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods 
Current control: the implementation of individual assignments and the organization of 
homework checking based on lecture materials in the form of computer tests. 
Final certification: exam.

name: Of the syllabus of the academic discipline
text:
ANNOTATION 
Of the syllabus of the academic discipline 
" Life Safety (Безопасность жизнедеятельности)" 
 
1. The name of the educational program within which the discipline is taught. The academic 
discipline is intended for undergraduate and specialty educational programs. 
 
2. Total labor intensity - 2 z 
 
3. The place of the discipline in the structure of the educational program  The academic 
discipline (module) “ Life Safety (Безопасность жизнедеятельности) ” refers to general university 
disciplines and is included in the mandatory part of the educational program. 
To study this academic discipline, you need knowledge, skills and abilities developed by 
previous disciplines: “Fundamentals of Life Safety”, “Mathematics”, “Physics”, “Chemistry”, 
“Biology”, “Social Studies”, “Ecology” in the scope of secondary school , as well as “Physical Culture 
and Sports” as part of the university program. Subsequent disciplines are determined according to the 
EP of a specific undergraduate (specialty) area. In general, successful study of the discipline allows 
students to take into account safety aspects in their professional activities and in everyday life during 
further studies. 
 
4. The purpose of studying the discipline:  the formation of a professional safety culture, 
which is understood as the willingness and ability of an individual to use in professional activities and 
in everyday life the acquired body of knowledge, skills and abilities to ensure safety, including in 
relation to persons with physical and (or) mental disorders; promote the formation of thinking and 
value orientations in which security issues are considered a priority, necessary to preserve human life 
and health, to preserve the natural environment, to ensure sustainable development of society, including 
in the event of the threat and occurrence of emergency situations and military conflicts. 
 
5. Requirements for the results of mastering the discipline.  The process of studying the 
discipline is aimed at forming elements of university -wide competencies of the SFU educational 
standard: 
Able to create and maintain safe living conditions in everyday life and professional activities to 
preserve the natural environment, ensure sustainable development of society, including in the event of 
the threat and occurrence of emergencies and military conflicts (УК-8). 
Competency indicators: 
1. Creates and maintains conditions for a safe, comfortable environment, including in the 
workplace and in everyday life (УК-8.1). 
2. Ensures its own safety, including in the event of emergencies and military conflicts ( УК-
8.2). 
3. Assess risk factors, including for the preservation of the natural environment, and is able to 
use personal and collective protective equipment (УК-8.3). 
4. Capable of implementing a set of protective measures in conditions of military operations 
(УК-8.4). 
Able to use basic defectological knowledge in the social and professional spheres (УК-11). 
Competency indicators: 
1. Focuses on the basics of basic defectological knowledge (УК-11.1). 
2. Applies basic defectological knowledge in the social and professional spheres with persons 
with physical and (or) mental disabilities (УК-11.2). 
 
6. The content of the discipline includes the study of the following modules: 
Module 1. Theoretical and methodological foundations of life safety. Theoretical foundations 
of BJD. Identification and impact on humans of harmful and dangerous environmental factors. 
Providing comfortable conditions for human life and activity. Ergonomic  fundamentals of safety. 
Information threats in the modern world. Information and psychological security of the individual. 
Features of interaction with persons with physical and (or) mental disabilities in the social and 
professional spheres. 
Module 2. Emergency situations and methods of protection in the conditions of their 
implementation. Phases of development of emergency situations. Emergency situations in peacetime 
and wartime and their damaging factors. Terrorism and terrorist activities. Methods for forecasting and 
assessing the situation in emergency situations. Unified state system for the prevention and liquidation 
of emergency situations. Fundamentals of organizing the protection of the population and personnel in 
peacetime and war. F irst aid techniques. Ensuring safety, especially protection from harmful and 
dangerous factors of natural, anthropogenic and man -made origin and organizing a rational and safe 
working environment for persons with physical and (or) mental disabilities. 
Module 3. Basics of military training. 
Basic provisions of the Military Doctrine of the Russian Federation. Fire training from small 
arms. Radiation, chemical and biological protection. Personal protective equipment and the procedure 
for their use. Medical support for troops (forces), first aid  for wounds, injuries and special cases. 
Military topography. 
 
7. Basic educational technologies . In organizing the learning process in the discipline “Life 
Safety”, traditional forms of education and innovative technologies are used. 
 
8. Forms of control - test.

name: Linear Algebra and Geometry (Линейная алгебра и геометрия)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
Introduction to Machine Learning and Neural Networks  
(Введение в машинное обучение и нейронные сети) 
Compiled by: Senior Lecturer of the Department of Informatics and Computational Experi-
ment N.N. Yachmeneva 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of preparation: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technolo-
gies (Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credits (180 hours), of which 36 hours of lectures, 36 hours of laboratory studies, 108 hours 
for independent study. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “Introduction to Machine Learning and Neural Networks (Введение в 
машинное обучение и нейронные сети)" (4 course, 7 semester) refers to the part of the block of 
disciplines (modules) formed by the participants of educational relations, and is an optional disci-
pline. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required that are 
formed by the previous undergraduate disciplines «Basics of Programming (Основы программи-
рования)», «Linear Algebra and Geometry (Линейная алгебра и геометрия) », «Programming 
Languages (Языки программирования)», «Computational Mathematics (Вычислительная ма-
тематика)» etc., in which the basic skills of creating complex programs are laid, and also gives an 
idea of modeling, optimization. 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to 
solve professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, 
when developing programs as part of the final qualification work. 
 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Development of a comprehensive view of students on a separate direction of development 
of artificial intelligence, based on a model of the human brain. The subject of discussion is various 
approaches and methods used in the field of machine learning and some neural networks. 
Tasks:  
• the study of the basic concepts of machine learning problems: a training sample, a model 
of algorithms, a training method, quality assessment, the problem of retraining and gener-
alizing ability of algorithms, a probabilistic formulation of a learning problem; 
acquaintance with some methods of solving problems of classification and regression; 
• mastering the technology of developing programs that use the main stages of the work of 
artificial neural networks - the creation of structures for representing neural networks, the 
creation of networks, their training, as well as the work of trained networks; 
• study of some methods of training neural networks, various network topologies, as well as 
problems for the solution of which networks are used; in addition, the network parameters 
are determined for the optimal solution of problems. 
 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, skills 
and abilities: 
To understand and analyze:  
• basic concepts of machine learning and neural networks: training set, object features, types of 
features, model of algorithms, data preprocessing, network topology, training method, model 
quality assessment, the problem of overfitting and generalizing ability of the algorithm 
• basic methods (algorithms) of machine learning; 
• the basic principles of developing programs that simulate the operation of neural networks; 
• main types of network topology;  
• basic methods of training neural networks and tuning them for optimal performance. 
To create and to be able to: 
• select and apply machine learning algorithms to specific tasks; 
• find the optimal parameters of algorithms for the task at hand, taking into account the selected 
quality metric 
• develop programs using ANN; 
• use suitable types of networks (backpropagation networks, convolutional networks, recurrent 
networks) to solve typical problems of artificial intelligence (problems of regression, recovery, 
recognition); 
• configure the basic parameters of neural networks, such as the number of network layers and 
neurons in layers, learning rate, activation functions, etc.; 
• use various objects for training in neural network applications: time signals, images. 
To apply: 
• in the application of machine learning technologies in solving practical problems. 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
 General professional competences (GIC) 
 OPK-3. Capable of developing algorithmic and software solutions in the fieldsystem and appli-
cation programming, mathematical, information and simulation models, the creation of infor-
mation resources of global networks, educational content, application dat abases, tests and testing 
tools for systems and tools for compliance with standards and initial requirements 
 Indicator 
 OPK-3.1. Applies methods of the theory of algorithms, methods of system and appliedprogram-
ming, fundamentals and concepts in the field of mathematical, information and simulation models 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Neural networks 
Topic 1.1. An introduction to artificial neural networks. ANN models. Learning pro-
cesses 
Definitions: neural network, properties of systems (nonlinearity, adaptability, etc.). Neu-
ron models, induced local field, types of activation functions. Network architecture: single -layer 
and multi -layer feedforward networks, recurrent networks. Knowledge  representation, rules of 
knowledge representation. Reducing the number of free network parameters. Neural network in-
variance. Various learning processes: learning based on error correction, learning based on 
memory, Hebb learning, competitive learning. The task of assigning confidence coefficients. Par-
adigms of learning neural networks: with and without a teacher. Learning objectives: pattern 
recognition, clustering, filtering, associative memory, function approximation, control. 
Neural network modeling tools. Python programming language and libraries Pandas, 
NumPy, Scikit learn, Tensorflow, PyTorch, (ml package) OpenCV. 
Topic 1.2. Multilayer perceptron 
Multilayer feedforward networks, signs of multilayer perceptrons, signal types. Backprop-
agation algorithm: forward and backward pass, derivation of the formula for correcting weights 
for hidden and output neurons (local gradient), types of activation functions, learning rate. Sequen-
tial and batch learning modes. Algorithm stopping criterion. Description of the backpropagation 
algorithm. Recommendations for improving the operation of the algorithm (maximization of in-
formation content, antisymmetry of the activation function, selection of target values, normaliza-
tion of inputs, initialization of weights, regularization). Generalization: retraining, factors of the 
ability to generalize. Sufficient training examples for correct generalization. Universal approxima-
tion theorem. Cross validation: model selection, early stop learning method. Methods to simplify 
the network structure: weight reduction, weight elimination, smoothing. Benefits and Limitations 
of Backpropagation Learning. Acceleration of convergence of t his method. Algorithm modifica-
tions. Discrepancy matrices. 
Topic 1.3. Convolutional and recurrent networks 
Working with images, their preprocessing, expanding the training sample. Forward and 
backward convolution. Subsampling with the determination of the maximum and average values. 
Convolution and subsampling layers, the role of fully connected layers in convolutional networks. 
Training of classifiers, performance evaluation. Deep convolutional networks. Incomplete train-
ing. 
Recurrent networks and neurodynamic programming. Hopfield network in the associative 
memory problem. Restricting the use of these networks. Hamming network. Bidirectional auto -
associative network, LSTM. Associative machines. Ensemble averaging. Amplificati on: strong 
and weak learning models, amplification due to filtering (3 experts), adaptive amplification algo-
rithm (due to subsampling). 
Section 2. Machine Learning 
Topic 2.1. Basic concepts 
Basic definitions: precedent, training sample, object attributes, types of attributes, matrix 
of object-attributes. Reducing the dimension of features. Algorithm model, teaching method. Es-
timating models. Selection of models. 
Topic 2.2. Basic algorithms 
Linear and nonlinear regression... Logistic regression (classification). Multi-class classifi-
cation.Building a decision list and decision tree. Tree reduction. Approximate calculation of the 
distribution density. Naive Bayesian classifier. One -dimensional and multidimensional cases. 
Generalized metric classifier. Types and features of special cases: methods of the nearest neighbor, 
k nearest neighbors, weighted neighbors. Support vector machine. SVM training. Compositions of 
algorithms. Examples: simple and balanced voting, bagging. Solving machine learning problems. 
 
Questions for self-study 
Separate tasks in laboratory work. Solving problems with real data. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies 
are used: 
- multimedia lectures 
- electronic forms of control 
- self-testing of students 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence -based learning, focused on 
the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
obtained. The deployment of a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, incl. application of the project-based teach-
ing method, technologies of guided self -study, including a point-rating system, as well as the in-
troduction of a system of online support for out-of-class work of students. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods 
Current control: laboratory work. 
Mid-term control: testing. 
Final certification: credit (pass/fail).

name: Computational Mathematics
text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
Computational Mathematics  
(Вычислительная математика) 
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Computational Mathematics and 
Mathematical Physics Tsyvenkova O.A. 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credits (180 hours), of which 32 hours of lectures, 32 hours of laboratory studies, 80 hours 
of independent work per semester and 36 hours of exam preparation. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Computational Mathematics (Вычислительная математика) " (2 
course, 4 semester) belongs to the compulsory part of the block of disciplines and is a compulso-
ry discipline. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by 
the previous disciplines “Basics of Programming (Основы программирования)", " Algebra and 
Geometry ( Алгебра и геометрия)" and " Continuous Mathematics ( Непрерывная 
математика)". 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to 
solve professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, 
in the development of algorithms and programs as part of the preparation of the final qualifica-
tion work. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Study of methods for the numerical solution of applied problems using a modern mathemat-
ical package. 
 
Tasks:  
• study of various methods for the approximate solution of problems of mathematical anal-
ysis, algebra and differential equations; 
• acquisition of practical skills in the implementation of computational algorithms; 
• developing the ability to conduct a computational experiment. 
 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, 
skills and abilities: 
To understand and analyze:   
• basic concepts of the theory of numerical methods for solving various problems of ap-
plied mathematics;  
• technologies for applying methods of computational mathematics to solving various 
problems; 
• basic algorithms for the implementation of computational algorithms by means of the 
Maple mathematical package; 
• basic techniques for verifying a computational algorithm 
To create and to be able to: 
• apply numerical methods to solve various problems in linear algebra, mathematical anal-
ysis and differential equations; 
• use the capabilities of the mathematical package for analyzing the problem, solving it and 
checking the result;  
• implement a computational algorithm for solving a specific problem using the Maple 
mathematical package 
To apply:  
• creating programs for solving applied problems by methods of computational mathemat-
ics 
... 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
  Professional competencies (ПК) 
  ПК -3. Capable of choosing a software architecture option, developing software for solving 
technical and research problems 
  Indicators 
  ПК -3.1. Based on the analysis of the requirements for the software product, it decomposes the 
software into components / software modules 
  ПК -3.2. Evaluates and selects design patterns (styles) for each layer or component 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Introduction. The error in the result of the numerical solution of the prob-
lem. Methods for determining the roots of a nonlinear equation. 
Topic 1.1. Sources and classification of error. Function error. 
Computational Mathematics Subject. Classification of computational methods. Computa-
tional Algorithm. Mathematical features of machine arithmetic. Types of errors. Sources of error. 
Absolute and relative error. Data recording forms. The error of basic arithmetic operations. 
Topic 1.2. Methods for solving algebraic and transcendental equations.  
Root separation methods (graphical and analytical). Half division method. Newton's 
method and its modifications. Choice of an initial approximation in Newton's method. Simple 
iteration method. 
 
Section 2. Construction of interpolation polynomials. Function approximation 
methods 
Topic 2.1. Interpolation polynomials in the form of Lagrange and Newton 
Statement of the interpolation problem. Lagrange interpolation polynomial, its unique-
ness, error estimate. Separated differences and their properties. Newton's interpolation polyno-
mials with separated differences. Solving problems of direct and inverse interpolation. Estima-
tion of the interpolation error. Reducing interpolation error. 
Topic 2.2 Least squares method for approximating functions 
Data approximation. Search for linear and quadratic functions. Nonlinear approximation, 
change of variables. 
 
Section 3. Methods for solving systems of linear and nonlinear equations. 
Topic 3.1. Direct and iterative methods for solving systems of linear algebraic equa-
tions. 
Direct and iterative methods, their advantages and disadvantages. Cramer's method. 
Gauss method. Inverse matrix method. LU -decomposition and its application to the solution of 
systems. Simple iteration method. Convergence condition Norms of vectors and matrices. Practi-
cal estimation of the error. 
Topic 3.2. Methods for solving systems of nonlinear equations of the second and 
higher orders. 
A system of two or more nonlinear equations, separation of roots. Newton's method. Ja-
cobi matrix. Practical estimation of the error. Simple iteration method for a system of nonlinear 
equations. Convergence conditions for the simple iteration method. 
 
Section 4. Methods of numerical integration and methods for solving the Cauchy 
problem 
Topic 4.1. Simple and compound quadrature formulas. Error estimation. 
Simple and compound quadrature formulas for rectangles, trapezoids and Simpson. Ge-
ometric illustration. Estimation of the error of quadrature formulas. Local and global integration 
error. Runge's rule for practical error estimation. 
Topic 4.2. Methods for solving the Cauchy problem 
Expansion in a series. Method of successive approximations. Explicit and Implicit Euler 
Methods. Runge's rule. Solution of systems of differential equations. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies are 
used: 
• multimedia lectures; 
• electronic forms of control; 
• self-testing of students. 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence -based learning, focused on 
the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
obtained. The deployment of a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, including the use of a project -based 
learning method, technologies of guided self -study, including a point -rating system, as well as 
the introduction of an online support system for students' out-of-class work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control: attending lectures, performing laboratory work. 
Mid-term control: performance of individual tasks. 
Final certification: exam.

name: Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика)
text:
ANNOTATION  
of the course  
Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика)  
 
Compiled by: Professor of the Department of Algebra and Discrete Mathematics Ya.M. Erusalim- 
sky  
 
1. Program title, degree, study mode  
Direction of training:  02.03.02 "Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technolo- 
gies"  
Qualification (degree) of the graduate:  bachelor  
Form of study:  full - time  
 
2. Total load  
9 credits (324 hours), of which 68 hours of lectures, 68 hours of practical training, 134 
hours o f independent work and 54 hours of exam preparation  
 
3. Course sequencing  
Academic discipline “ Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика) ”  refers to the man- 
datory part of the discipline block. To study this academic discipline, knowledge in mathematics, 
computer science and the basics of ICT acquired in secondary school is required.  
The list of subsequent academic disciplines for which knowledge, skills and abilities are 
required, formed by this academic discipline:  
“ Mathematical Logic (Математическая лог ика) "," Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная 
математика) "," Automata Theory and Formal Languages (Теория автоматов и формальных 
языков) "," Algorithms and Data Structures (Алгоритмы и структуры данных) ","  Expert Sys- 
tems and Non - classical Logic (Экспертные систем ы и неклассические логики) ” , “ Probability 
Theory and Mathematical Statistics (Теория вероятностей и математическая статистика) ”  and 
others.  
4. Course aims and objectives  
Developing students' competencies in using the apparatus of discrete mathematics in so lv- 
ing their professional problems.  
Tasks:  
-  Assistance in the formation of a comprehensively developed personality as a subject of 
successful professional, educational and research activities.  
-  Formation of students' understanding of the place of discrete mathematics in the system 
of mathematical disciplines and their applications, of its connections with algebra, geometry, 
mathematical analysis, probability theory and mathematical statistics, computer cycle disci- 
plines, etc.  
-  Formation of professional competencies of a bachelor, associated with the use of mathe- 
matical models of processes and objects, the development of effective mathematical methods for 
solving discrete problems.  
 
5. Intended learning outcomes  
As a result of mastering the d iscipline, the student must:  
Know : basic concepts and objects of discrete mathematics: statements and operations on 
them, predicates and operations on them, including quantifiers, sets and operations on them, 
basic combinatorial concepts, fundamentals of t he theory of mappings, general theory of Boole- 
an functions, graphs and networks.  
Be able to : to carry out equivalent transformations of the formulas of the algebra of state- 
ments, to construct the normal forms of the algebra of statements, to synthesize an d simplify the 
r. - c. circuits and circuits of functional elements, solve combinatorial problems of basic types, 
work with Boolean functions, analyze sets of Boolean functions for completeness, find local and 
global characteristics of graphs, apply Kruskal and Dijkstra's algorithms, build graph matrices.  
Own : instrumental means and methods of discrete mathematics and the ability to apply 
them in solving practical problems.  
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following comp e- 
tencies:  
  General professional competences  
  ОПК - 1. Able to apply fundamental knowledge gained in the field of mathematical and (or) natu- 
ral sciences, and use them in professional activities  
  Indicator  
  ОПК - 1.1. Applies the basic provisions and concep ts in the field of mathematical sciences and 
basic terminology in solving problems of professional activity  
 
6. Course content  
Module 1. Propositional algebra  
Statements. Operations on statements: negation, disjunction, conjunction, equivalence, and 
their simplest properties.  
Dependencies between operations. Equivalence in propositional algebra. Boolean proposi- 
tional algebra. Formulas in propositional algebra. Substitution and equivalent substitution theo- 
rems.  
Duality in propositional algebra. The principle  and law of duality . Normal forms. The main 
problems of propositional algebra: equivalence, resolution, representation.  
Relay - contact circuits and circuits of functional elements. Analysis, synthesis, simplifica- 
tion of circuits. Binary adder. Analysis of the performance of single - digit and multi - digit adders.  
Module 2. Algebras of predicates and sets  
Predicates and Quantifiers. The concept of a predicate. Examples of predicates. Logical 
operations on predicates. Boolean predicate algebra. Quantifiers and t heir properties. Application 
of the language of predicates and quantifiers.  
Algebra of sets. The concept of a set and an element of a set. Universal and empty sets. 
Sets and unary predicates. Operations on sets: addition, union, intersection, difference an d sym- 
metric difference. Boolean algebra of sets. Subset. Families of sets.  
Module 3. Mappings. Combinatorics. Relations  
Mappings. Examples of mappings. Image and preimage of a set when displayed. Properties 
of images and prototypes. Composition of mappings . Types of mappings: injective, surjective, 
bijective, "none".  
Composition of mappings of the same type (theorems on the composition of mappings of 
the same type). Reversibility and one - sided invertibility of mappings. Criteria for reversibility 
and one - wa y reversibility .  
Combinatorics. The basic principle of combinatorics. The number of elements in a finite 
set. Sum rule. Inclusion - exclusion formula. Cartesian product of sets. The number of elements in 
the Cartesian product.  
Sets of injective and bijective  mappings. Placements and permutations.  
Combinatorics. Combinations, binomial Newton. Combinations with repetitions. The 
number of surjective maps.  
Relations. Examples of relationships. Boolean operations on relations. Boolean algebra of 
relations. Boolean  matrices. Boolean algebra of 0 - 1 matrices.  
Binary relationships. Properties of binary relations. Examples of relationships with various 
combinations of properties. Order relationships and dominance.  
Equivalence relation. Equivalence classes and their prop erties. Factor set.  
Module 4. Boolean Functions  
Boolean functions. The sets P 2 ( n ) , P 2 ... Theorem about | P 2 ( n ) | = 2 
2 
n 
... Set analy- 
sis P 2 ( 2 ) ... Schaeffer's stroke and Pierce's arrow. Zhegalkin polynomials.  
Completeness and isolation. Post Classes P 0  and P 1 and their properties. Classes L,  S, M 
and their properties. Post's completeness theorem (completeness criterion) and its consequences.  
Precomplete classes and their properties. Existence of precomplete classes.  
Module 5. Theory of algorithms. Turing machine  
What is an "algorithm"? Exampl es of algorithms. Alphabet, letters, words. Writing a word 
on a tape. The simplest operations on words. Turing machine. Addition of numbers in the unary 
number system.  
Special Turing machines: identical, replacing, copying. Composition of Turing machines. 
Machines with semi - belts. Combining Turing machines.  
Forking and iterating machines. Universal alphabet, universal encoding. Algorithmic de- 
cidability and algorithmic undecidability. Universal Turing Machine.  
Module 6. Fundamentals of Graph Theory  
The subje ct of graph theory. Graph definitions. Examples of graphs. Local characteristics 
of graphs. Graph isomorphism. Geometric graphs. Correct implementation of the graph. Correct 
implementation theorem in R 3 ... Plane and non - planar graphs. The concept of the Pont ryagin - 
Kuratovsky criterion. Paths, chains, contours, cycles. Connected and tightly connected compo- 
nents.  
Parts of a graph: subgraph, partial graph. Bridges and points of articulation. Bridge theo- 
rem. Euler graphs. Eulerian criterion. Trees and forests. Ma rked trees. Enumeration of marked 
trees.  
Graph matrices: matrix of adjacency, incidence, cuts, cycles. The theorem on the rank of 
the incidence matrix. Spaces of cycles and cuts and their dimensions. Orthogonality ratio.  
Algorithms on graphs: finding components and bicomponents, bridges and points of articu- 
lation, condensation. Kruskal's algorithm, Dijkstra's algorithm. Streams in networks.  
 
7. Basic educational technologies  
When conducting classes, such educational techno logies are used as classical lectures, 
problem lectures; work in small groups -  performing tasks in the classroom with a preliminary 
collective discussion of the topic; individual tasks (home and classroom).  
Classroom and extracurricular work is organized on the basis of an individual and differen- 
tiated approach to students. The educational process is based on the concept of competence - 
based learning, focused on the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating 
the theoretical knowledg e obtained. The deployment of a competence - based learning model in- 
volves the widespread use of innovative ways of organizing the educational process, incl. appli- 
cation of the project - based teaching method, technologies of guided self - teaching, including th e 
point - rating system.  
 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control:  homework.  
Mid - term control:  test papers.  
Final examination:  exam.

name: Foreign Language for Business Communication (Russian)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
"Foreign Language for Business Communication (Russian)  
(Иностранный язык для деловой коммуникации (русский))" 
Compiled by E.B. Popkova, Associate Professor of the Department of the Russian Language for 
Foreign Students  
1. Total load disciplines - 4 credits, 144 hours. 
2. Course sequencing:  The academic discipline "Foreign Language for Business 
Communication (Russian)" refers to a part of the block of disciplines (modules) formed by 
the participants of educational relations, and is an optional discipline. To study this 
academic discipline, the following knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by 
the previous disciplines: 
Knowledge: a system of basic linguistic concepts, including grammatical and word -
formation phenomena, basic lexical units of a terminological nature, intercultural and 
collective interaction. 
Skills: the use of linguistic means to achieve the communicative goals of interpersonal and 
intercultural communication. 
Skills: knowledge of a foreign language in oral and written form for the implementation of 
communication in the socio-cultural. 
 
The program is designed for students who have completed the Foreign Language (Russian) 
training course, who, according to the international standard of proficiency in a given 
foreign language, have reached level B1 - the third level of language proficiency in the 
Common European System CEFR, a system for determining various language levels 
compiled by the Council of Europe. 
 
Course aims and objectives: Basic  the goal of the " Foreign Language for Business 
Communication (Russian) (Иностранный язык для деловой коммуникации (русский)) " 
course at the undergraduate level is to acquire the necessary and sufficient level of 
communicative competence for students to solve social and communicative problems in various 
areas of business, cultural, professional and scientific activities when communicating with 
foreign partners, as well as for further self-education.  
Tasks: foreign language courses at the undergraduate level are based on the principles of 
personality-oriented, competence -based and modular -rating approaches and allow taking into 
account the needs and interests of students. Thus, the objectives of the course for teaching a 
business foreign language include: 
• increasing the level of educational autonomy, the ability to self-education; 
• development of cognitive and research skills; 
• development of information culture; 
• the ability to navigate in formal business and scientific styles; 
 
Along with the practical goal, this course also implements educational goals: increasing the 
general culture of students and the formation of competencies in accordance with the OS of 
the SFedU in this area of training (specialty): 
 
 Universal Competencies (УК) 
 
 
 
 
 УК-4. Able to carry out business communication in oral and written forms in the state language 
of the Russian Federation and foreign language (s) 
 Indicators 
 УК-4.2. Perceives, analyzes and evaluates oral and written information of a personal and 
academic nature in Russian and foreign language (s) 
 УК-4.3. Conducts correspondence in a foreign language, taking into account the peculiarities of 
the style of business communication 
 УК-4.5. Performs translation of official and professional texts for personal purposes 
Course content:  Teaching Russian language proficiency in oral and written form for 
communication in the professional and socio -cultural spheres of communication is carried 
out during 2 semesters (6 modules): 
Module 1. From the history of scientific discoveries 
Study discussion on the topic "The greatest inventions that changed our lives " 
Conversation on the topic "Unexpected discoveries" 
Reading and discussion of the text "Intellectual emigration"  
Monologue saying "Technological progress: good or evil?" 
Grammar: Expressing target relationships in simple and complex sentences. 
 
Module 2. The contribution of scientists to the development of science 
Educational discussion on the topic "What should be a modern scientist" 
Reading and conversation on the topic "How to get the Nobel Prize" 
Monologue saying "Soviet and Russian Nobel Prize winners" 
Written statement on the topic "The moral responsibility of scientists for their discoveries." 
Grammar: constructions with verbs of reciprocal meaning. 
 
Module 3. Learn always, learn everywhere 
Study discussion on "Libraries - Past or Future?" 
Reading and discussion of the test "Problems of modern education" 
Monological statement "Modern sources of information" 
Written statement - "How I see the education of the future" 
Grammar: Expressing Comparative Relationships 
 
Module 4. Science and education in the 21st century 
Viewing and discussion of a fragment of a TV show on the channel "Culture" on the topic of the 
module 
Educational discussion on the topic "University of the XXI century: how and what to teach" 
Reading and discussing the Productive Power of Science test 
Written statement - "My profession in 30 years" 
Grammar: active and passive constructs 
 
Module 5. Mobile technologies in science and education 
Project (presentation) "Internet technologies in education: pros and cons". 
Viewing and discussing a fragment of a TV show on the Culture channel on the topic of the 
module. 
Reading and discussing the Science and Morality test. 
Written statement "Mobile technologies when writing a term paper." 
Grammar: Expression of Comparative Relations. 
 
Module 6 International scientific forums and summits 
Viewing and discussion of a fragment of the "News" program on the topic of the module 
 
 
 
 
Educational discussion on the topic "How to prepare an interesting report for a scientific forum" 
Monologue statement "Necessary personal qualities, skills and abilities for public speaking" 
Writing abstracts for participation in a student conference 
Role-play game on the topic "At the high-tech exhibition" 
Grammar: expressing concessions 
 
Additional useful information: The program covers the first stage of the course (part 2) of 
teaching the Russian language at the university, the level of preparation of a bachelor / graduate, 
i.e. 3-4 courses. Successful mastering of the program presupposes the achievement of the B1 / 
B2 level "intermediate / above average" in Russian, ie. the formation of linguistic 
communicative competence, sufficient to study foreign experience in the chosen direction of 
training. As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must: 
Know: various forms and types of communication for use in specific areas, situations and 
conditions of communication;  
Be able to: understand texts of a personal and academic nature; to perceive by ear within the 
limits of the literary norm on topics related to the educational and professional interests of the 
student; participate in discussions on topics of level B1 and above of the Russian system of 
levels of proficiency in Russian as a foreign language. 
Own: normative pronunciation and basic grammar for the implementation of oral and written 
communication within the framework of educational topics, skills of dialogical and monologue 
speech, skills of abstracting, annotation (in accordance with the level B1 and higher of the 
Russian system of levels of proficiency in Russian as a foreign language) 
To achieve the set goals of the discipline " Foreign Language for Business Communication 
(Russian) (Иностранный язык для деловой коммуникации (русский)) ", the following 
educational technologies are used: conversation, discussion and discussion, role -playing 
games, maintaining a student "portfolio", presentations using multimedia technologies, 
scientific student, conducted in English, release wall newspapers and stands in English for 
various dates and significant events.  
Assessment tools for monitoring progress include current, midterm control and intermediate 
certification. 
 
Monitoring forms  - tests and assignments conducted in individual, pair and group forms 
(oral questioning in dialogical and monologue form; writing a message on the proposed 
topic (essay); presentations). 
Forms of midterm control - lexical and grammatical tests. 
Intermediate certification  - credit in the 5th semester, differential credit in the 6th 
semester.

name: Foreign language (Иностранный язык)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
" Foreign language (Иностранный язык)" 
 
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Russian Language for Foreign Students, 
Ph.D. A.A. Grigoryan 
 
1. Total load disciplines - 12 ZET, 432 hours. 
2. Course sequencing: The academic discipline "Foreign Language (Russian)" for natural 
science areas of training belongs to the mandatory part of the block of disciplines (modules)...  
3. Course aims and objectives: 
The main goal of the "Foreign language (Иностранный язык)" discipline isshaping the ability to 
carry out business communication in oral and written forms in the state language of the Russian 
Federation, to master the system of norms of the Russian literary language, to perceive, analyze 
and evaluate oral and writt en information of a personal and academic nature in Russian, the 
ability to reasonably, logically correctly and meaningfully build oral and written speech, 
demonstrating personal and professional culture, fluency in Russian to solve communication 
problems in all spheres of communication.  
To achieve this goal, it is necessary to form a foreign language communicative 
competence, which is part of the professional competence of a bachelor at the B1 level. 
(document State educational standard in Russian as a fo reign language of the first certification 
level (general knowledge) ... Foreign language communicative competence is considered as the 
ability to effectively participate in foreign language oral and written communication in the 
context of intercultural communication.  
To achieve this goal, it is necessary to solve the following tasks in each of the semesters. 
Tasks mastering the discipline in the 1st semester: 
- adjustment, activation and expansion of language knowledge and speech skills acquired 
during pre-university training (according to the Standard of the first certification level of general 
language proficiency); 
- mastering the most frequent grammatical constructions and lexical units of the scientific 
style of speech; development of primary speech ski lls based on general scientific and special 
texts; 
- the formation and development of skills in studying and introductory reading on a 
selected topic with the subsequent extraction of information from the text necessary in the 
process of communication; 
- development of listening skills, phonetically correct appearance of the Russian word 
and phrase, expansion of the systemic understanding of the phonetic system of the Russian 
language and its functioning. 
Tasks mastering the discipline in the 2nd semester: 
- activation of existing and the formation of new linguistic knowledge and speech skills; 
- assimilation of knowledge about the functioning of the Russian language in different 
spheres of communication, perception and comprehension of information in vario us styles of 
speech, including scientific and educational and popular science substyles; 
- expansion of knowledge about the structural features and linguistic content of the text, 
the formation and development of skills for constructing written speech statements in the 
educational, professional and business spheres of communication; 
- the formation and development of the ability to convey the content of the source text 
with a given degree of convolution, the development of the ability to reflect the sequence of 
presentation of thoughts, the ability to generalize what has been read or said - drawing up plans 
of various types, taking notes of the read or heard text, as well as the formation of the ability to 
restore the content of the source, the ab ility to deploy information the basis of the plan and other 
supports.

name: Computer Graphics (Компьютерная графика)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
Computer Graphics (Компьютерная графика) 
Compiled by: 
Associate Professor of the Department of Higher Mathematics and Operation Research N.V. 
Danilova 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Qualification (degree) of the graduate: bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
7 credits (252 hours), including 54 hours of lectures, 54 hours of laboratory classes and 108 
hours for independent work during the semester and 36 hours for preparing for the exam. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Computer Graphics (Компьютерная графика) " (4th year, 7th se-
mester) refers to a part of the block of disciplines (modules) formed by participants in education-
al relations, and is a mandatory discipline. 
To study this academic discipline (module), knowledge, skills and abilities are required, 
which are formed by the previous disciplines “ Basics of Programming (Основы 
программирования)”, «Linear Algebra and Geometry (Линейная алгебра и геометрия) ”, 
“Calculus (Непрерывная математика) ”, “ Algorithms and Data Structures (Алгоритмы и 
структуры данных)”. 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to 
solve professional problems in research, research, production and design activities, in particular, 
in the development of algorithms and programs as part of the preparation of the final qualifica-
tion work. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Study of modern methods and technologies of computer graphics programming. 
Tasks: 
• studying the principles of software development used to create (synthesis) and edit imag-
es, as well as to digitize visual information obtained from the real world for the purpose 
of its further processing and storage; 
• acquisition of skills in the development of algorithmic and software solutions in the field 
of computer graphics problems, including the use of mathematical, information and simu-
lation models, mathematical information models; 
• mastering the technology of developing programs for creating (synthesis) and editing im-
ages, as well as for digitizing visual information received from the real world for the pur-
pose of its further processing and storage; 
acquisition of skills in working with libraries that implement a platform-independent 
programming interface for writing applications that use two-dimensional and three-dimensional 
computer graphics (based on OpenGL). 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
To understand and analyze: 
• the basic principles of software development used both for creating (synthesis) and 
editing images, and for digitizing visual information received from the real world 
for the purpose of its further processing and storage; 
• principles of operation of programs for creating (synthesis) and editing images; 
• basic computer graphics algorithms; 
• the main features of libraries for writing applications that use two -dimensional and 
three-dimensional computer graphics (on the example of OpenGL). 
To create and to be able to: 
• develop and implement computer graphics algorithms; 
• use the possibilities of libraries for writing applications that use two -dimensional 
and three-dimensional computer graphics; 
• develop programs using shaders; 
• in the application of computer graphics programming technologies. 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competencies: 
        General professional competences (ОПК) 
ОПК -6. Able to understand the principles of operation of modern information technologies and 
use them to solve problems of professional activity 
        Indicator 
ОПК -6.1. Understands the principles of modern information technology 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Raster and vector 2D graphics 
Topic 1.1. Introduction to computer graphics. Basic concepts and definitions of raster 
graphics 
Basic concepts and definitions. 
Topic 1.2. color models. Color Space Conversions 
color models. color space. Halftone and binary images. 
Topic 1.3. Raster Algorithms 
Border selection algorithm. Algorithm for filling with preliminary border selection. Re-
cursive fill algorithm based on a series of pixels (lines). Comparison of fill algorithms. Bresen-
heim's algorithm for drawing lines. Wu's algorithm for drawing lines. 
Topic 1.4. Affine transformations on the plane. Auxiliary vector algorithms 
Affine transformations on the plane and in space. The orientation of the point relative to 
the segment. Determination of the point of intersection of two segments. Edge rotation. Distance 
from a point to a line. Check if a point belongs to a convex polygon. Check that a point belongs 
to an arbitrary polygon - the angle method. Check that a point belongs to an arbitrary polygon - 
the ray method. 
Topic 1.5. Vector algorithms for 2D graphics: construction of convex hulls, tri -
angulation, operations with polygons. 
Construction of a convex hull when entering points step by step. Construction of a con-
vex hull by Graham's bypass method. Construction of a convex hull using the “gift wrapping” 
method (Jarvis). Merging two convex hulls. Triangulation of an arbitrary polygon using the 
method of invading vertices. Triangulation of an arbitrary set of points by the Delaunay method. 
Triangulation of a monotone polygon. Splitting a non -monotone polygon into monotone ones. 
Intersection of 2 convex polygons. Union of 2 convex polygons. Difference of 2 convex poly-
gons. 
Topic 1.6. Construction of fractal images. 
Fractals. Classification. Construction. Application in computer graphics. L -systems. The 
diamond-square algorithm. Systems of iterated functions. 
Topic 1.7. Visualization of curves and surfaces. Geometric splines 
Curves and surfaces. Representation of curves on a plane. Representation of surfaces. 
Bezier curves in plane and space. Properties of Bezier curves. Compound cubic Bezier curve. 
Rational Bezier curves. Inhomogeneous rational B -spline, NURBS. Bezier surfaces. Bicubic 
Bezier surface: conjugation. 
Section 2. Modeling and visualization of three -dimensional objects. Ray tracing algo-
rithms for realistic images.  
Topic 2.1. Affine transformations in space. Types of design 
Affine transformations in space. Types of design. Types of 3D models, data structures for 
their storage. Construction of 3D models: extrusion, rotation figures. 
Topic 2.2. Removing Hidden Lines and Surfaces 
Trimming non-front faces. Z-buffer. Ray tracing. Plotting a function of two variables. 
Topic 2.3. Rasterization. Lighting. Texturing 
Local and global lighting models. Phong model. Rasterization. Fill in Fong and Guro. 
lighting models. Ray tracing: ray casting. Texturing (face, sphere, cylinder). 
Topic 2.4. Ray tracing algorithms for realistic images. 
Ray tracing algorithms: ray tracing. Data structures and implementation algorithms. 
Section 3. Real-time imaging. opengl. 
Topic 3.1. Leading in OpenGL. 
opengl. Application structure. Command syntax. Examples of state variables. State man-
agement. Rendering. Render pipeline. opengl. 
Topic 3.2. Output in OpenGL. Composition of objects. materials and lighting. 
Coordinate transformations. Working with matrices. View transformations. Projections. 
Output area. Composition of objects. The sequence of transformations. opengl. materials and 
lighting. material properties. Sources of light. Point source parameters. Directional source pa-
rameters. Spotlight source parameters. 
Topic 3.3. Texturing in OpenGL. Loading a texture from a file and software generation. 
Texturing: texture dimensions; texture mapping steps. Loading models. Meshes. Formats 
for storing models. OBJ format. COLLADA format. 
Topic 3.4. Introduction to shaders. GLSL language. 
Shaders. Concept. Kinds. Application. shader languages. GLSL. Data types. control 
structures. Built-in global variables. Shader examples. 
Topic 3.5. Vertex and index buffers (VBO). Examples and debugging GLSL 
shaders.debug. 
Vertex and index buffers (VBO). Examples and debugging of GLSL shaders. Debugging 
shaders. 
Topic 3.6. Formats for storing models. Meshes. Loading realistic models. 
Formats for storing models. Meshes. Loading realistic models. .obj and .collada formats. 
Topic 3.7. Lighting models and their implementation in shaders. 
Shaders for lighting calculations. Phong lighting. Lighting models and their implementation 
in shaders. 
Topic 3.8. Embossed texturing. 
Embossed texturing. Types of relief texturing. bump mapping. normal mapping. displace-
ment mapping. parallax mapping. 
Topic 3.9. Shadow overlay 
Shadow rendering. Building shadows with shadow maps.  
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies are 
used: 
• multimedia lectures; 
• electronic forms of control; 
• self-testing of students. 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence-based learning, focused on the 
formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
received. The deployment of a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, including the use of the project-based 
learning method, guided independent learning technologies, including a score-rating system, as 
well as the introduction of an online support system for students extracurricular work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods 
Current control: performance of laboratory and individual works. 
Boundary control: testing. 
Final certification: exam.

ANNOTATION of the course  
Computer Networks (Компьютерные сети) 
 
Compiled by S.A. Guda, Associate Professor of the Department of Algebra and Discrete 
Mathematics 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor

2. Total load 
6 credits (216 hours), of which 48 hours of lectures, 32 hours of laboratory studies, 82 hours

3. Course sequencing

refers to the compulsory part of the discipline block. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by the 
previous disciplines «Basics of Programming (Основы программирования)» , «Computer Ar-

The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to

4. Course aims and objectives

Tasks:

puter networks

name: Mathematical Logic (Математическая логика)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
Mathematical Logic (Математическая логика) 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of preparation: 02.03.02 "Theoretical Computer Science and Information Tech-
nologies" 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
6 credits (216 hours), of which 54 hours of lectures, 36 hours of practical training, 87 hours 
for independent work and 39  hours for exam preparation. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline (module) “ Mathematical Logic (Математическая логика) " (2nd 
year, 3rd semester) belongs to the basic part of the professional cycle and is a compulsory disci-
pline. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by 
the previous discipline “Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика)". 
The list of subsequent academic disciplines for which knowledge, skills and abilities are 
required, formed by this academic discipline: “Automata Theory and Formal Languages (Теория 
автоматов и формальных языков)", "Algorithms and Data Structures ( Алгоритмы и структу-
ры данных)", "Expert Systems and Non -classical Logic ( Экспертные системы и неклассиче-
ские логики)". The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be 
used to solve professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in 
particular, when developing programs as part of graduation qualification works. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Developing students' competencies related to the use of classical logics, mastering the 
skills of constructing logical inference in such logics as propositional calculus and predicates of 
the Hilbert and Gentzen types. 
Tasks:  
• studying the principles of constructing and using classical logics (using the example of 
propositional calculi and predicates of the Hilbert and Gentzen types), in which standard 
methods of reasoning are formulated, such as the conclusion of a contradiction, infer-
ence from the opposite, etc.; 
• mastering the technology of formalizing statements formulated in a natural language, as 
well as in terms of a mathematical language in which many natural science disciplines 
are described (for example, continuous mathematics); 
• the study of various methods for checking the deducibility of statements, such as meth-
ods of reduction, Quine and operative inference; 
• studying the possibilities and features of logical programming languages that use the 
method of resolutions (Robinson) in predicate calculus to solve various problems. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, 
skills and abilities: 
To understand and analyze:  
• the basic terms of classical logics - propositional calculi and predicates, formulated by 
Gentzen and Hilbert; 
• the relationship between the specified calculus, namely, their equivalence; 
• basic rules of inference and axioms of calculus; 
• the main ways of constructing the derivation of statements of calculus;  
• the main theorems establishing a connection between true and deducible statements, as 
well as decidability, consistency and independence of classical calculi; 
• knowledge of the main characteristics of the studied calculi (decidability, inconsistency, 
independence) and problems; 
• knowledge of the features of using various algorithms for checking the validity and in-
consistency in theorem proving; 
• syntax of logical languages of the Prolog family (for example SWIProlog, Visual 
Prolog); 
• applied problems that can be effectively solved using logical languages of the Prolog 
family; 
• understanding the essence of the resolution method in predicate calculus, its role in log-
ical programming languages. 
To create and to be able to: 
• analyze the subject area, identify the main objects and connections between them, as 
well as formalize them in terms of predicate calculus or statements; 
• build inference of statements using inference rules and axioms; 
• build a conclusion of statements from cause to effect (output from top to bottom) and 
from consequence to axioms (output from bottom to top);  
• use appropriate methods to test the deducibility of assertions; 
• develop programs using logical programming languages; 
• establish links between a formal language (information or syntax) and its interpretations 
(real objects), identify unambiguous or ambiguous definiteness of syntactic and semantic 
objects, carry out classification (i.e. build theories). 
To apply:  
• in identifying causal relationships between objects in various subject areas; 
• in the possession of the technique of logical transformations, especially the handling of 
quantifiers; 
• use of languages of the Prolog family in problem solving. 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
 ОПК-1. Able to apply the fundamental knowledge gained in the field ofmathematical and (or) 
natural sciences, and use them in professional activities 
 Indicator 
 ОПК-1.1. Applies the basic provisions and concepts in the field of mathematical sciences and 
basic terminology in solving problems of professional activity 
 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Propositional calculus of Gentzen type (sequential calculus) 
Topic 1.1. Definition of sequential propositional calculus 
The subject of study is mat. logic. Definition of calculus, inference rules, calculus theo-
rems, calculus language. Gentzen -type propositional calculi (IS). Alphabet, formulas IC. A pro-
posal for a uniquely representable form of the IC formula. IC sequences, sequence schemes, axi-
oms. IP withdrawal rules. 
Topic 1.2. Output to the IS in the form of a tree. Valid rules. Equivalent formulas 
Linear proof, IS theorems. Inference tree in IS. Proposal for the proof of IS theorems. 
Examples of the output of formulas. Valid IP rules, tantamount to. Equivalent formulas: substitu-
tion in IS, substitution theorem, 3 lemmas on equivalence of formulas, substitution theorem. 
Topic 1.3. Normal forms. Interpretation of IP. IS completeness theorem. IP properties 
Normal forms, basic equivalences in IS, letters, clauses, reduction to DNF and CNF. 
Semantics of IS: interpretation of IS, theorem of interpretation, consistency of IS, main interpre-
tation, identically the truth of formulas and sequences. Connection between provable and identi-
cally true formulas, IS completeness theorem, decidability and independence of IS. 
Section 2. Propositional calculus of Hilbert type and algorithms for checking 
the validity and inconsistency of formulas in IV 
Topic 2.1. Description of IV. Deduction theorem. The link between IS and IOT 
IW of the Hilbert type: Alphabet, formulas, inference, axiom schemes, inference rules, 
hypotheses, examples of formula derivation. The deduction theorem, its application to the deri-
vation of formulas. The theorem on the equivalence of IS and IV. 
Topic 2.2. Methods for checking the general validity of formulas in IV for the applica-
tion of the completeness theorem 
Algorithms for checking the general validity and inconsistency of formulas in IW. 
Quine's algorithms, reductions, examples. Clause resolution, resolution proposition, theorem on 
the completeness of the resolution method. Resolution method for Horn clauses. Conjunction 
method for conjuncts. 
 
Section 3. Predicate calculus (PI) 
Topic 3.1. Algebraic systems. Signature formulas. Sequential predicate calculus 
Signature, signature algebraic systems, examples. SP: alphabet, signature terms, formu-
las of signature Σ, examples of formulas. Free variables, closed formulas (sentences). Validity of 
signature formulas, examples. Executable, generally valid formulas, examples, a theorem on the 
creation of generally valid and contradictory formulas. Model of a set of formulas. Sequential 
ISS Σ: alphabet, axioms, inference rules, examples of derivation of formulas, proposals for prov-
ing ISS theorems, on substitution. Valid rules. The relation 
 , the truth of the sequences in the 
algebraic system. Consistency theorem for ISP Σ. Equivalence of formulas in ISS Σ, proposition-
ally equivalent formulas, equivalence propositions, replacement theorem. 
Topic 3.2. Normal forms. IP Hilbert type 
Normal forms, DNF, CNF, preclasual normal form, examples of how to obtain PCNF. 
ISΣ: alphabet, formulas, axioms, inference rules, deduction theorem, proposition on relations 
with quantifiers, theorem on the equivalence of ISSΣ and ISΣ. 
 
Section 4. Model theory and proof theory 
Topic 4.1. Application of the method of resolutions in IP. Unification of terms 
Model existence theorem, Gödel completeness theorem. Locally satisfiable sets of for-
mulas, theorems on locally satisfiable sets. Axiomatic classes. Skulemization of an algebraic sys-
tem: enrichment of AS, Skulem's axioms, Skulemization Σ, AS, Skolem functions, Complete 
skulemization of systems. Clasual normal form. Gentzen's system G. Comparison of it with the 
predicate calculus. Herbrand's theorem. Method of resolutions in IP: Substitutions, unifiers, the 
most common unifier, many mismatches. Algorithm for unification. Binary resolvent of formu-
las, resolvent of clauses, Theorem on the completeness of the method. Application of the method 
of resolutions in programming: logic programs, facts, rules of purpose, example. 
Topic 4.2. Elementary theories 
Elementary equivalence of AS, elementary systems theory. Elementary System Exten-
sion A proposal for an elementary extension. Elementary theories. Consistency, completeness, 
system of axioms for theory, examples.
 -formulas, 
 -formulas, 
 -formulas, axiomatizable 
theories associated with them, proposition about axiomatizability. T -equivalence, theory with 
elimination of quantifiers, examples. Conservative extension, 2 types of extensions. Peano's sys-
tem of axioms, the standard model of elementary arithmetic. A proposal for some properties de-
duced from the Peano system of axioms. 
 
Questions for self-study 
Non-classical logics. Modal, temporary, fuzzy, algorithmic logics. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and practical classes, the following educational technologies 
are used: 
- lectures 
- hometasks 
- electronic forms of control 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence -based learning, focused on 
the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
obtained. The deployment of a competence-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, incl. application of the project -based 
teaching method, technologies of guided self -study, including the point-rating system, as well as 
the introduction of an online support system for students' out-of-class work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control: implementation of practical work, colloquium. 
Midterm control: execution of control works. 
Final certification: exam.
