ANNOTATION of the course 
Mathematical Foundations of Information Security 
(Математические основы защиты информации)  
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Algebra and Discrete Mathematics 
Mogilevskaya N.S. 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technolo-
gies (Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credits (180 hours), of which 32 hours of lectures, 32 hours of practical training, 62 hours 
for independent work, 54 hours for exam preparation. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Mathematical Foundations of Information Security 
(Математические основы защиты информации)" (3 course, 6 semester) refers to a part of a 
block of disciplines (modules) formed by participants in educational relations, and is a compul-
sory discipline. 
To study this academic discipline (module), knowledge, skills and abilities are required 
that are formed by the previous disciplines “ Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics 
(Теория вероятностей и математическая статистика)” , « Discrete Mathematics 
(Дискретная математика)», « Linear Algebra and Geometry (Линейная алгебра и 
геометрия)». 
The list of subsequent academic disciplines for which knowledge, skills and abilities are 
required, formed by this academic discipline: “ Coding Theory ( Теория кодирования)". The 
knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to solve pro-
fessional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, in the 
development of algorithms and programs as part of the final qualification work. 
 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Objectives assimilation disciplines: the development of students' competencies related 
to the setting of problems and the most important results of number theory, general algebra and 
information theory, which will later serve as a basis for other training courses and be used in 
the graduate's practical work. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, 
skills and abilities: 
To understand and analyze:  
• basic concepts and facts of algebra and number theory at the level required by an infor-
mation technology specialist; 
• basic functions of number theory; 
• methods for solving comparisons and applications of these methods in programming 
problems; 
• algorithms for finding prime numbers and testing numbers for simplicity; 
• basic concepts of information theory; 
• basic algorithms for coding information for transmission over a channel with limited 
bandwidth; 
• basic concepts of cryptography.   
To create and to be able to: 
• build a mathematical and computer construction of an arbitrary Galois field; 
• use methods and means of number theory to solve information security problems; 
• use number-theoretic algorithms to implement public key cryptographic algorithms; 
• build a practical implementation of the basic codes. 
To apply:   
• work with objects of general algebra, number theory and information theory. 
 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following compe-
tencies: 
 ОПК-1. Able to apply fundamental knowledge gained in the field of mathematical and (or) 
natural sciences, and use them in professional activities 
 Indicator 
 ОПК-1.3. Solves standard math problems and applies their solutions in professional activities 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Algebraic Foundations protection andinformation 
Topic 1.1. Divisibility in a ring of integers. 
Ring. Division lemma with remainder. Divisibility relation. Greatest common divisor. 
Euclid's Algorithm. Mutually prime numbers. Least common multiple. Prime numbers. Proper-
ties of prime numbers. The main theorem of arithmetic. Canonical decomposition of a number. 
Topic 1.2. Comparisons.  
Comparability ratio. Comparison properties, classes of numbers for a given module. 
Complete and reduced deduction systems. Euler's and Fermat's theorems. Existence and 
uniqueness theorem for solution of first degree congruence, solution algorithm. A system  of 
comparisons of the first degree with one unknown. Legendre and Jacobi symbols. Comparisons 
of the second degree. 
Topic 3.1. Algebraically structure. 
Groups, rings, fields. Definition, examples. Invertible elements, multiplicative group of 
a ring. Zero divisors, irreversibility of zero divisors. Examples of fields. Subring. A ring of 
polynomials over an arbitrary field. Division with remainder. Field ch aracteristic. Subfield. 
Simple field. Different representations of the Galois field. Calculations over Galois fields. Ex-
istence theorem for Galois fields. Existence theorem for an irreducible polynomial of arbitrary 
degree over a finite field. 
 
Section 2. Information theory and cryptography 
Topic 2.1 Entropy, discrete stationary source. 
Basic definitions. Joint entropy. Conditional entropy.Discrete stationary source, discrete 
constant source. Different approaches to defining the measurement of information. Information 
on Hartley. Factor classes and information. Information on Fitingof. A theorem on the entropy 
characteristics of a discrete stationary source. The concept of coding, uniform code, uniform 
code speed. Direct theorem of (uniform) coding of a discrete constant source. 
Topic 2.2. Uneven coding, basic codes. 
Uneven coding. Uniquely decoded and prefix codes. Craft's inequality. Direct and con-
verse theorems of non -uniform letter-by-letter coding. Huffman, Shannon and Gilbert -Moore 
codes. Arithmetic coding. Lempel-Ziv algorithms. 
Topic 2.3. Cryptosystems. 
Definition of a cryptosystem. Shift codes, substitutions, permutations. Affine cipher. 
Cryptanalysis of a simple substitution cipher. Vigenère cipher. Permutation cipher. Attacks on 
cryptosystems, the Kerkhoffs principle. The concept of cryptanalysis of th e Vigenere cipher. 
Hill's cryptosystem, attacks on it 
Topic 2.4. Resilience of cryptosystems. 
The absolute strength of the shift cipher. Shannon's theorem. The key is unreliable. False 
keys, distance of uniqueness. 
Topic 2.5. Number-theoretic algorithms for information security. 
Cryptosystem RSA. Attacks on RSA. Nightingale -Strassen test. Cryptosystem of El 
Gamal. Discrete logarithm, Pollig-Hellman algorithm. Plotting large primes. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and practical laboratory exercises, the following educational 
technologies are used: 
- multimedia lectures 
- electronic forms of control 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence-based learning, focused 
on the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical 
knowledge obtained. The deployment of a competency -based learning model involves the 
widespread use of innovative ways of organizing the educational process, incl. application of 
the project-based teaching method, tec hnologies of guided self -teaching, including the point -
rating system. 
 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Midterm control: control works. 
Final certification: exam.

name: ОСНОВЫ РОССИЙСКОЙ ГОСУДАРСТВЕННОСТИ
text:
Annotation of the course  
«ОСНОВЫ РОССИЙСКОЙ ГОСУДАРСТВЕННОСТИ» 
 
1. Total labor intensity: 2 ZET (72 hours) 
2. Place of discipline in the structure of the educational program 
The academic discipline “Fundamentals of Russian Statehood” belongs to the compulsory 
part of the program of the 1st semester of the 1st year. 
To study this academic discipline, you need knowledge, skills and abilities formed by the 
disciplines: History, Social Science, Russian Language. Mastering this discipline is necessary for 
the formation of a developed sense of citizenship and patriotism in students, the formation of their 
leadership position in students, the development of initiative and social activity. 
3. The purpose of studying the discipline  is to form in students a system of knowledge, 
skills and competencies, as well as values, rules and norms of behavior associated with the 
awareness of belonging to Russian society, the development of a sense of patriotism and 
citizenship, the formation of  the spiritual, moral and cultural foundation of a developed and 
integral personality , aware of the peculiarities of the historical path of the Russian state, the 
originality of its political organization and the c onnection of individual dignity and success with 
social progress and political stability of its Motherland. 
The implementation of the course requires students to consistently master knowledge, 
ideas, scientific concepts, as well as historical, cultural, sociological and other data related to the 
development of Russian civilization and its statehood in historical retrospect and in the context of 
current challenges of political, economic, man-made and other nature. 
4. Contents of the discipline 
Section 1. What is Russia. The country in its spatial, human, resource and ideological and 
symbolic dimensions. 
Section 2. Russian state - civilization. Historical, geographical, institutional foundations 
for the formation of Russian civilization. Conceptualization of the concept of “civilization” 
Section 3. Russian worldview and values of Russian civilization. Worldview and its 
significance for a person, society, state 
Section 4. Political structure of Russia. An objective presentation of Russian state and 
public institutions, their history and key cause -and-effect relationships of recent years of social 
transformation 
Section 5. Challenges of the future and development of the country. Scenarios for the 
country's future development and the role of the citizen in these scenarios 
5. Additional useful information in studying the discipline 
In the process of teaching the academic discipline “Fundamentals of Russian Statehood,” 
traditional, innovative, active and interactive technologies are used. Particular emphasis is placed 
on interactive educational technologies: the use of multimedia pres entations; analysis of specific 
situations (case method); business games and scenario modeling techniques; open discussions and 
student debates; access to multimedia educational portals; viewing current educational and artistic 
videos; organization of “rou nd tables”, etc. The course is focused on the developmental 
educational paradigm, according to which the student does not just receive a certain amount of 
information from the teacher, but is in the process of active learning, independent search, mastering 
information and knowledge, skills and abilities in the course of studying the subject.

text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
Parallel and Multithreaded Programming (Параллельное и 
многопоточное программирование) 
 
Compiled by M.E. Abrahamyan, Associate Professor of the Department of Algebra and Dis-
crete Mathematics 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credits (180 hours), of which 36 hours of lectures, 36 hours of laboratory studies and 108 
hours of independent work 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Parallel and Multithreaded Programming ( Параллельное и 
многопоточное программирование)” (4th year, 7th semester) refers to the part of the block of 
disciplines (modules) formed by the participants of educational relations, and is an optional disci-
pline. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, formed by the 
previous disciplines “Basics of Programming (Основы программирования)" and "Computer Ar-
chitecture and Operating Systems (Архитектура компьютера и операционные системы)". 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to solve 
professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, in the 
development of algorithms and programs as part of the preparation of the final qualifying work. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Study of modern methods and techniques of parallel and multithreading programming. 
Tasks: 
• study of the basic means of parallel programming: the MPI library and the OpenMP pro-
gramming interface; 
• acquaintance with the basic techniques for parallelizing computational tasks; 
• acquisition of skills for creating, running and debugging parallel programs using specialized 
tools; 
• acquisition of user and programming skills for working with a computing cluster. 
 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, abili-
ties and skills: 
To understand and analyze: 
• basic paradigms of interaction of computing processes, 
• principles of functioning of parallel programs; 
• basic principles of the technology for the development of parallel programs based on mes-
sage passing; 
• the main features of the MPI library related to message passing and collective interaction of 
parallel processes; 
• additional features of the MPI library related to the definition of new user data types and 
their packing, work with process groups and communicators, the use of virtual topologies; 
• principles of technology for the development of parallel programs based on the use of shared 
memory; 
• OpenMP software interface; 
• basic parallel algorithms related to numerical integration (grid algorithms), processing of 
matrices and systems of linear equations (matrix algorithms), modeling the interaction of sets of 
particles. 
To create and to be able to: 
• use modern software implementations of the MPI library (in particular, the MPICH software 
package) for the development of parallel programs; 
• use various tools of the MPI library to solve typical tasks related to parallel programming; 
• use various means of the OpenMP interface to solve typical tasks related to parallel program-
ming; 
• work with a computing cluster. 
To apply: 
• in the use of standard tools for the development and launch of parallel programs. 
 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
ПК-3. Capable of choosing a software architecture option, developing software for solving 
technical and research problems 
Indicators 
ПК-3.3. Develops procedures and integrates software modules and components 
ПК-3.4. Performs assessment and selection of coding style and data access technology 
 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Introduction to the parallel calculations. Developing of distributed applications by 
means of the MPI technology 
Topic 1.1. Overview multiprocessor systems programming tools. MPI Technology: a gen-
eral description 
Basic architectures of multiprocessor systems: shared memory systems, distributed memory 
systems. The methodology for developing a parallel program (Y . Foster). Examples of implemen-
tations of parallel programs to calculate a definite integral: branching (fork / wait), multithreading 
based on POSIX Pthread and Thread object, OpenMP library, distributed computations based on 
the PVM and MPI interfaces, High Performance Fortran language (HPF). The history of develop-
ment and the versions of the MPI interface (Message Passing Interface). The basic MPI notions: a 
process, a communicator, a message sender and a message receiver, MPI runtime. The MPICH 
system and the electronic book of educational training tasks Programming Taskbook for MPI. 
Topic 1.2. Point-to-point communication. Collective communication 
Six basic functions of MPI. Timing functions. Blocking and non-blocking point-to-point com-
munications. Communication modes: the standard mode, synchronous mode, the buffered mode, 
the ready mode. Receiving messages and related functions including MPI_Probe  and 
MPI_Get_count. Deadlocks during the blocking communications and how to avoid them. A non -
blocking receiving messages and the Wait and Test family of functions. Receiving messages from 
any source (MPI_ANY_SOURCE) and receiving messages with any tag (MPI_ANE_TAG). Com-
bined send-receive operations and their features. Collective communications and their main dif-
ferences with the point -to-point communications. Barrier synchronization via the MPI_Barrier 
function. The types of collective communications: broadcasting communication MPI_Bcast, gath-
ering data to one member MPI_Gather and MPI_Gatherv, gathering data where all members re-
ceive the result MPI_Allgather and MPI_Allgatherv, scattering data to all me mbers MPI_Scatter 
and MPI_Scatterv, combined scattering / gathering data from all to all members MPI_Alltoall and 
MPI_Alltoallv. Collective communications with a varying count of data for each process, their 
features. 
Topic 1.3. Global reduction operation. Derived datatypes. Packing and unpacking 
The predefined reduction operations, the specific features of the MPI_MINLOC and 
MPI_MAXLOC operations. The types of possible reduction operations: receiving the result data 
in one process MPI_Reduce, receiving the result data in all processes MPI_Allreduc e, combined 
reduction and scattering the results data to all processes MPI_Reduce_scatter, the prefix reduction 
MPI_Scan. Derived MPI datatypes and their characteristics: the extent (the MPI_Type_extent 
function) and the size (the MPI_Type_size function). Datatype constructors: replication of a 
datatype into contiguous locations (MPI_Type_contiguous), replication of a datatype into loca-
tions that consist of equally spaced blocks (MPI_Type_vector and MPI_Type_hvector); replication 
of a datatype into a sequence of blocks, where each block can contain a different number of copies 
and have a different displacement (MPI_Type_indexed and MPI_Type_hindexed); replication of 
a datatype into a sequence of blocks, where each block consists of different datatypes 
(MPI_Type_struct). Derived datatypes committing and releasing. Using the derived datatypes for 
the efficient sending of two -dimensional data blocks. Packaging and unpackaging data via the 
MPI_Pack and MPI_Unpack functions, their features. Sending of packed data (the MPI_PACKED 
datatype). Packaging and unpackaging data via the MPI_Pack and MPI_Unpack functions, their 
features. Sending of packed data (the MPI_PACKED datatype). Packaging and unpackaging data 
via the MPI_Pack and MPI_Unpack functions, their features.  Sending of packed data (the 
MPI_PACKED datatype). 
Topic 1.4. Groups of processes and communicators. Virtual topologies 
Predefined groups of processes; group constructors: create a new groups of processes on the 
basis of an existing ones or on the basis of the communicator, using a set operations for groups. 
Predefined communicators; communicator constructors: create a new communicator on the basis 
of existubg groups and using the MPI_Comm_split function for splitting of the existing commu-
nicator. Communicators' comparing. The use of new communicators for execution of collective 
operations within the part of existing process es. Communicators with the topology. Types of to-
pologies: the Cartesian topology and the graph topology. Constructors for communicators with the 
topology. Cartesian topology with periodicity in some dimensions. Additional features of commu-
nicators with the Cartesian topology: rank-to-coordinates and coordinates-to-rank translation, the 
data shift for a given coordinate (non-periodic or periodic), partitioning of Cartesian communicator 
into communicators with low-dimensional Cartesian topology. Additional features of communica-
tors with the graph topology: providing the information about the neighbors of a certain process 
(adjacency information for a graph topology). 
Section 2. Developing multi-threaded applications using OpenMP 
Topic 2.1. OpenMP Programming Interface: a general description 
OpenMP interface and its versions. Model of the OpenMP program. The compiler mode with 
the OpenMP support. OpenMP directives and routines (functions). Parallel parts of the OpenMP-
program. Shared and local variables in the OpenMP -program. Setting the param eters of the 
OpenMP-program via environment variables, OpenMP functions, and clauses of the OpenMP di-
rectives. Timing functions. 
Topic 2.2. The basic means of parallelization in OpenMP 
Low-level parallelization via omp_get_thread_num () and omp_get_num_threads (). Parallel 
sections, their features. Directives for single-thread execution. Parallelization of loops, its features. 
The schedule clause and schedule types for load balancing (st atic block distribution, dynamic 
block distribution with fixed-size blocks and guided block distribution with variable-size blocks). 
Topic 2.3. The synchronization means in OpenMP 
The importance of synchronization for parallel programs with shared memory. Critical sec-
tions and their usage (the critical directive). The barrier synchronization (the barrier directive). The 
assignment synchronization (the atomic directive). An example o f ineffective and effective syn-
chronization of the implementation of the parallel algorithm for finding the maximum or minimum 
value. 
Section 3. Parallel algorithms in numerical methods. Development and implementation of 
parallel programs on computer clusters 
Topic 3.1. Overview architectures of multiprocessor computer systems 
Flynn classification of computer systems. Vector-conveyor supercomputers. Symmetric multi-
processor system (SMP). Systems with a massive parallel processing (MPP). Clustered systems. 
The effectiveness of parallel programs. Amdahl's law. Load balancing. Parallel programs with the 
shared memory: problems arising in connection with the cache memory. Accounting the commu-
nication environment properties (bandwidth and latency) for parallel programs with the distributed 
memory. 
Topic 3.2. The parallel matrix algorithms 
Using the MPI technology to implement a big matrices multiplication. The band matrix mul-
tiplication algorithms. The block matrix multiplication algorithms (the Fox algorithm and the Can-
non algorithm), features of their implementation (using the derived datatypes, communicators with 
the Cartesian topology, collective communications). 
Topic 3.3. Parallel methods of solving boundary value problems of mathematical physics 
The Dirichlet problem for the Poisson equation, non-parallel versions of its numerical solution 
(the Gauss-Seidel method and the Gauss-Jacobi method). Parallel algorithms for solving the prob-
lem using OpenMP technology: two variants of the Gauss-Seidel method. Eliminating the mutual 
influence of the parallel threads: a parallel variant of the Gauss -Jacobi method; Gauss -Seidel 
method with the alternation of odd and even rows; wave algorithm and problems with its effi-
ciency. Parallel algorithms for solving the problem using MPI technology: the band algorithm of 
the Gauss-Seidel method. Features of the band algorithm (using communicators with the Cartesian 
topology and various types of collective communications). 
Topic 3.4. Parallel methods of solving n-body problem 
N-body problem, its mathematical model and non -parallel version of its numerical solution. 
Parallel algorithms for solving the problem that use a shared memory without and with the load 
balancing, a comparison of their efficiency. Parallel algorithms for s olving the problem that use 
messaging: the “manager -workers” model, the pulse model, the conveyor model, their software 
implementation. 
Topic 3.5. Running programs on a Unix cluster 
The Unix-systems properties. Organization of the file system; files and processes. Command 
executing on a Unix system. Commands for working with directories, files, and processes. Using 
the Midnight Commander file manager on Unix -based servers. Remote work  with Unix-based 
servers: programs for Windows-based client (the PuTTY terminal program, the FAR file manager 
and its using for files transfer); configuring of the PuTTY program; communication with the server 
and authorization. Compilation of parallel programs on Unix-based servers, including the compi-
lation of programs using MPI. The parallel program running in several nodes of the cluster using 
the job scheduling system PBS (Portable Batch System). 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies are 
used: 
• multimedia lectures; 
• electronic forms of control; 
• self-testing of students. 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence -based learning, focused on 
the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
obtained. The deployment of a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, including the use of a project-based learn-
ing method, technologies of guided self -study, including a point-rating system, as well as the in-
troduction of an online support system for students' out-of-class work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods 
Current control: attending lectures, performing laboratory work. 
Mid-term control: testing, completing additional tasks. 
Final certification: credit, set based on the results of work in the semester.

name: Scientific Computing Software (Maple, MatLab) (Программное
text:
ANNOTATION  
of the work program of the academic discipline 
Scientific Computing Software (Maple, MatLab) (Программное 
обеспечение для научных вычислений (Maple, MatLab))  
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate's qualification (degree): Bachelor's degree 
Form of study: full-time form  
2. The total labor intensity  
6 credits (180 hours), including 54 hours of lectures, 18 hours of laboratory classes, 108 
hours of independent work. Exam 
3. Course sequencing 
The academic discipline «Scientific Computing Software (Maple, MatLab)» ( 4 year of 
Bachelor program, 7th semester) refers to parts of a block of disciplines (modules) formed by 
participants in educational relations and is an elective discipline. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge and skills formed by the following disciplines 
studied in the un dergraduate program are necessary: Discrete Mathematics ( Дискретная мате-
матика)», « Linear Algebra and Geometry (Линейная алгебра и геометрия) », « Calculus 
(Непрерывная математика) », «CS101. Basics of Programming ( Основы 
программирования)». 
The knowledge and skills acquired during the study of this discipline can be useful in solv-
ing professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, as well as in 
preparation for final qualification work. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Form the competencies of imitation and super computer modeling with the help of 
computational software packages Maple and Matlab, learn to use these software packages for 
scientific computing and solving applied problems. 
Main aims: 
• Study the syntax, elements of programming, graphical toolbox and algorithms of themat-
ic GUI construction.  
• Study the tools designed for the functions analysis, problems of differential and integral 
calculus 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student is expected to have the following 
knowledge, skills and abilities: 
 
To understand and analyze: 
• Syntax and commands of the software packages; 
• Graphical features; 
• Software packages functionality for solving applied problems. 
 
To create and to be able to: 
• Use the advantages of specific Maple packages and Matlab Toolboxes;  
• Select effective algorithms for solving the problem of scientific computing. 
To apply: 
• Performing scientific research using the Maple and Matlab packages.  
 
• The process of discipline studying forms the following competencies: 
 
ПК-2. Ability to develop custom and standard technical documents.  
Indicators 
ПК-2.1. Creation of operational documents for users of the computer system; 
ПК-2.2. Development of technical documents in accordance with the given standards; 
ПК-2.3. Formation of electronic Help in a standard format, as well as demonstration mate-
rials 
 
6. Course content 
 
Module 1. Mathematical software package Maple  
Topic 1. Maple basics 
 
1.1 The main functionality of the Maple system. Package structure and interface. Data types 
and structures. Standard functions. Converting objects. 
1.2 Creating user’s functions in Maple. Solving algebraic equations and inequalities. 
1.3. Graphical 2D,3D objects. Animation are optional. 
Topic 2. Mathematical analysis and Linear Algebra in Maple 
2.1. Fundamentals of mathematical analysis in Maple. Calculation of limits and derivatives. 
Research of functions. Differentiation and integration operations. Decomposition of functions 
into series and functions approximation.  
2.2 Basic functionality of linear algebra packages. Properties of matrices, SLAE solution. 
 
Topic 3. Programming and solving differential equations in Maple 
3.1 Programming elements. Creation of procedures, modules, libraries. Exchange operations 
(Input/Output).  
3.2. Elements of differential calculus. Construction of an analytical solution, approximate 
solution, including numerical solution of the ordinary differential equations ( ODE) and partial 
differential equations (PDE). Systems of differential equations. Cauchy problem. The using  
built-in graphical interpretation of solution. 
 
Module 2. Computational software package MatLab  
Topic 4. Basic functionality of the MatLab system. 
4.1. Package structure. Interface. Interactive and programmatic operation. Instructions for remote 
work in https://www.mathworks.com/ 
4.2. Basic classes of ML-objects. Hierarchy. Command window. Operations with basic objects.  
4.3. Matrix constructors. Operations with matrices. Elements of linear algebra, matrix properties 
(eigenvalues, eigenvectors, norms and so on). Arrays of Char or Strings, arrays of Cell. Type 
control functions. Converters. 
4.4. Functions, script files (*.m), procedures. Functions with an arbitrary number of arguments. 
Anonymous. Programming elements. Efficient algorithms. 
Topic 5. Graphical functionality. Solving problems of linear algebra and mathematical 
analysis. 
5.1. Graphics. Basic primitives, high-level commands and descriptive graphics. Operating with 
graphic objects (2D and 3D). Multi-windows graphics. Animation. 
5.2 Problems of linear algebra. Investigation of matrix properties. Complete, sparse systems of 
linear algebraic equations (SLAE), factorization methods.  Effective methods of SLAE solving.  
5.3. Elements of differential and integral calculus. Symbolic and numerical integration and 
differentiation. Research of functions. Solving nonlinear equations and systems of equations.  
5.4. Principles and methods of a graphical user interface (GUI) construction.  
 
Topic 6. Imitation and supercomputer simulation in Matlab.  
 
6.1 Possibilities for simulation and supercomputer modeling in Matlab. An overview of Matlab 
application packages.  
6.2 Fundamentals of simulation modeling for solving optimization problems using the Neural 
Network Toolbox module in Matlab. Step-by-step instructions for formalizing the task, 
simulating the process of construction a solution, and adjusting parameters.  
 
Questions submitted for independent study

text:
ANNOTATION of the course

Zemlyakova Irina Alexandrovna, Cand. Sc. (Physics and Mathematics), Senior Lecturer of

3. Course sequencing 
The discipline «Modern optimization methods (Современные методы оптимизации)» (3 
course, 6 semester) refers to the mandatory part of the block of disciplines and is mandatory. 
To study this academic discipline, knowledge, skills and abilities are required, which are 
formed by the disciplines " CS102. Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика) ", "CS103. 
Algebra and Geometry (Алгебра и геометрия) ", " CS104. Continuous Mathematics 
(Непрерывная математика) ", " CS292. Computational Mathematics (Вычислительная 
математика)", «CS291. Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics (Теория вероятностей и 
математическая статистика)». 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to 
solve professional problems in research, research, production and design activities. 
 
4. Course aims and objectives 
To prepare students for the analysis of processes and phenomena in the search for optimal 
solutions, apply the acquired knowledge in solving practical problems, form professional 
competencies that contribute to successful work in the chosen field. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following 
competencies: 
 
ОПК-3. Capable of developing algorithmic and software solutions in the field of system and 
application programming, mathematical, information and simulation models, creating information 
resources of global networks, educational content, application databases, tests and means of testing 
systems and tools for compliance with standards and initial requirements 
Indicators: 
ОПК -3.1. Applies methods of the theory of algorithms, methods of system and applied 
programming, basic provisions and concepts in the field of mathematical, information and 
simulation models 
ОПК -3.2. Correlates programming knowledge, defines and creates information resources of 
global networks, educational content, system testing tools 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Optimization problems in machine learning 
Subject 1.1. Optimization approach in machine learning 
Optimization problems in machine learning. Optimization in supervised learning. Bayesian 
optimization. Bayesian optimal classification. Bayesian optimization through binary classification. 
Optimal feature selection. Isolation of signs through gradation of relations. Feature extraction 
through clipping of ensembles. Vector ranking metrics. 
Topic 1.2. Sparse machine learning methods 
Linear / logistic regression models with L1 and L1 / L2 regularizations. The concept of the 
subgradient of a convex function, its connection with the directional derivative, a necessary and 
sufficient condition for an extremum for convex nonsmooth problems  of unconstrained 
optimization. Steepest subgradient descent method. Proximal method. Method of coordinate 
descent and block coordinatewise optimization. 
 
 Section 2. Stochastic Optimization 
Topic 2.1. Optimization Techniques Using Parameter Dependent Global Upper 
Bounds 
Probabilistic linear regression model with different regularizations: quadratic, L1, Student. 
The idea of an optimization method based on the use of global estimates, convergence. An example 
of the application of the method for teaching LASSO. Constructi on of global estimates using 
Jensen's inequality, EM -algorithm, its application for probabilistic linear regression models. 
Constructing estimates using tangents and variable substitution. Jaakkola -Jordan estimate for the 
logistic function, estimates for t he Laplace and Student distributions. Applying estimates to train 
probabilistic linear regression models. Convex-concave procedure, examples of use. 
Topic 2.2. Stochastic optimization 
General formulation of the stochastic optimization problem, an example of use. The tasks 
of minimizing the average and empirical risk. Stochastic gradient descent method, two phases of 
the iterative process, using averaging and inertia. Stochastic Gradient Descent as an Optimization 
Method and as a Learning Method. SAG method. Applying stochastic gradient descent for SVM 
(PEGASOS algorithm).

• self-testing of students.

organizing the educational process, including the use of a project -based learning method, technologies of 
guided self-study, including a point-rating system, as well as the introduction of an online support system 
for students' out-of-class work.

istic finite automata; study of the general scheme of the machine-recognizer; mastering the 
method of reducing a non -deterministic automaton to a non -deterministic one; mastering 
the methods of constructing a finite automaton using a regular grammar; studying the prop-
erties of right-linear, regular and automatic languages; 
• mastering the concept of a finite state machine with spontaneous transitions; mastering the 
methods of constructing a finite automaton according to a right-linear grammar and calcu-
lating the language of a finite automaton using sequential elimination of st ates; study of 
the concepts of equivalence relation on the set of finite automata, unattainable states of an 
automaton; 
• studying the problem of minimizing a deterministic finite automaton; mastering the con-
cepts of distinguishable and indistinguishable states and the method of constructing a sys-
tem of relations of indistinguishability of states of a finite automaton; mastering the meth-
ods of determining the regularity of the language; study of algorithmic problems of regular 
languages; 
• mastering the mathematical foundations of the theory of context -free (CS) languages; the 
study of the concepts of the inference tree in KS-grammar; mastering the methods of check-
ing the CS-grammar for non-emptiness, constructing a stabilization set using the CS-gram-
mar, constructing the reduced CS-grammar; the study of the normal forms of Chomsky and 
Greibach KS-languages; mastering the method of determining the belonging of the chain 
to the language, given by the KS-grammar; 
• mastering the mathematical foundations of the theory of automatic machines with store 
memory (MP-machines); study of the concept of non -determinism for MP -automata, an 
extended form of an MP -automaton (MP-automaton), an automaton that admits language 
by emptying the store (MPε-automaton); mastering the methods of transition from an MP-
automaton to an MPε-automaton and vice versa; mastering the method of constructing an 
MPε-automaton using the CS-grammar; mastering the method of transition from an MP ε-
automaton to a CS-grammar. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, skills 
and abilities: 
To understand and analyze:  
• basic principles for defining finite formal descriptions of potentially infinite languages;  
• the principles of the functioning of finite state machines and the construction of finite state 
machines using grammars and regular expressions; 
• properties of regular expressions and languages; 
• basic types of state machines;  
• main methods of optimization of finite state machines. 
To create and to be able to: 
• determine the type and compose formal grammars of languages from verbal descriptions;  
• build finite state machines based on verbal descriptions, regular expressions and formal 
grammars; 
• apply algorithms for reducing grammars, constructing normal forms of grammars, check-
ing the language specified by the grammar for nonempty;  
• solve the problems of minimizing finite automata, computing the language of a finite au-
tomaton, belonging of a chain to a language; 
• build finite automata for recognizing CF languages, find CF grammars corresponding to a 
given finite automaton. 
To apply:  
• in the application of methods of the theory of automata and formal languages. 
 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
  Universal Competencies (УК) 
  УК-1. Able to search, critically analyze and synthesize information, apply a systematic approach 
to solving assigned tasks 
  Indicator 
  УК-1.1. Carries out search, selection, systematization, generalization and critical analysis of in-
formation 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Foundations of the theory of formal languages. Regular languages and ex-
pressions 
Topic 1.1. Introduction to the theory of formal languages. Basic concepts and defini-
tions. Grammars and languages generated by grammar 
Alphabet. The words. Operations on words. Prefixes and suffixes, subwords. The degree 
of the word. Word length. Examples. Language over the alphabet A. Empty language. Language 
A *. Language A +. Operations on languages. Examples. 
Topic 1.2. Chomsky's classification of formal languages. The task of parsing words, 
types of conclusions in grammar, equivalence of conclusions, ambiguity of grammars 
Grammar. Output words. A language generated by grammar. Examples. Equivalent and 
nearly equivalent grammars. Chomsky's classification of formal languages. Examples. Parsing 
words. Left and right word conclusions. Equivalence of conclusions. Output tree. Examples. Am-
biguity of KS-grammar. 
Topic 1.3. General scheme of the automaton-recognizer. Regular sets and regular ex-
pressions. Regular Expression Lemma 
Algorithmic model of a finite automaton - recognizer. Software implementation of a regular 
language recognizer. Drawing up a finite -automaton program based on PL -grammar. Defining a 
regular set and a regular expression. Properties and basic techniques of r egular expression trans-
formations. 
Topic 1.4. Finding the smallest fixed point of a system of linear equations with regular 
coefficients 
Linear Equations with Regular Coefficients. Least Fixed Point Theorem. Systems of linear 
equations with regular coefficients. Algorithm for constructing the smallest fixed point of a system 
of linear equations with regular coefficients. 
Topic 1.5. Lemmas on the right-linearity of elementary languages and operations on 
PL-languages. Lemma on the regularity of PL-languages 
Definitions of elementary languages. Search for right-linear grammars for elementary lan-
guages. Search for grammars that implement basic operations on right -linear languages: union, 
concatenation, iteration. The form of the smallest fixed point of a system of linear equations with 
regular coefficients. 
Section 2. Finite state machines. Algorithmic Problems of Regular Languages 
Topic 2.1. Basic principles of working with state machines 
State machines: configuration, reachable states, clock. A language defined by a state ma-
chine. Determinism and non-determinism of finite state machines. Reduction of NCA to DCA. 
Topic 2.2. Coincidence of classes of regular, right-linear and automaton languages 
Lemma on the right-linearity of finite automata. Lemmas on the automatism of elementary 
languages and operations on languages. A theorem on the coincidence of the classes of regular, 
right-linear and automaton languages. 
Topic 2.3. A finite automaton with ε-transitions 
A finite state machine with spontaneous transitions: configuration, reachable states, clock. 
E-closure of an ε-NFA state, Lemma on the reduction of an ε-NFA to a DFA. Construction of ε-
NCA according to right-lined grammar. 
Topic 2.4. Definition of the ε-NCA language 
Computing the ε-NFA language by the method of sequential elimination of states. Convert 
regular expression to ε-NFA. 
Topic 2.5. Equivalence relation on the set of finite automata 
Unattainable states of ε-NCA. Elimination of unattainable states. Lemma on the relation of 
indistinguishability of a DFA state. 
Topic 2.6. DFA minimization 
Lemma-definition of the system of relations of indistinguishability of states by words of i 
letters. DFA minimization algorithm. DFA minimization theorem. 
Topic 2.7. Boolean algebra of regular languages 
A theorem on the properties of regular languages. Closedness under union, intersection, 
and complement operations. Growth lemma for regular languages. The problem of non-emptiness, 
belonging and equivalence of languages. 
Section 3. Context-free languages and store-bought machines 
Topic 3.1. Derivability in CS grammars 
Output trees in KS grammars. Section of a tree. The crown of the tree. Section Lemma. 
The krone lemma. Corollary theorem from lemmas. Algorithm for checking the CS -grammar for 
nonempty. Correctness theorem for the algorithm. 
Topic 3.2. Unreachable and useless symbols in the CS grammar 
Algorithm for constructing a stabilization set based on the CS -grammar. Barren symbols 
of KS-grammar. Algorithm for elimination of unattainable symbols from KS-grammars. Algorithm 
for eliminating useless symbols from KS-grammars. 
Topic 3.3. Non-shortening KS grammars 
Algorithm for converting KS -grammars to a non-shortening form. Chain products in KS 
grammars. KS grammars without loops. Algorithm for removing chain products. 
Topic 3.4. Given KS grammars 
Algorithm for converting KS-grammars to a reduced form. Chomsky's normal form of KS-
grammars. Algorithm for converting KS-grammars to Chomsky normal form. 
Topic 3.5. The canonical form of Greibach KS-grammars 
Systems of constitutive equations. The smallest fixed point. Correspondence between the 
set of systems of defining equations and the set of KS-grammars. The normal form of the Greibach 
KS-grammar. The theorem on the least fixed point of the system of governing equations. 
Topic 3.6. MP-machines 
Configuration. Achievable states. Tact. Non-determinism of the MP -automaton. The lan-
guage determined by the MP machine. 
Topic 3.7. MPε-automata 
The language allowed by the automaton emptying the store. MP ε-automaton. Algorithm 
for constructing an MPε-automaton from the CS-grammar. Algorithm for constructing a KS-gram-
mar from an MPε-automaton. 
Questions for self-study 
State machine optimization. The problem of belonging for KS -languages. Coca -Younger-
Kasami algorithm. Matrix representation of systems of constitutive equations. Algorithm for con-
verting KS-grammar to Greibach normal form. RMP-machines. Configuration. Achievable states. 
Tact. Nondeterminism of the RDM -automaton. The language defined by the RDM machine. Al-
gorithm for constructing an MP-automaton from an MPε-automaton. Equivalence of MP-automata 
and CS-grammars: an algorithm for constructing an RDM-automaton using CS-grammar. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies 
are used: 
- lectures 
- hometasks 
- self-test of students 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence -based learning, focused on 
the formation of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge 
obtained. The deployment of a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of 
innovative ways of organizing the educational process, incl. application of the project-based teach-
ing method, technologies of guided self -study, including a point-rating system, as well as the in-
troduction of a system of online support for out-of-class work of students. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control: attending lectures, working in practical classes, completing additional tasks. 
Midterm control: control work, colloquium. 
Final certification: exam.

name: Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics (Теория
text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics (Теория 
вероятностей и математическая статистика) 
 
 
Compiled by: Head of the Department of Differential and Integral Equations, Doctor of 
Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Associate Professor O.G. Avsyankin 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credits (180 hours), of which 36 hours of lectures, 36 hours of practical training, 36 hours 
for exam preparation and 72 hours for independent work. 
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics (Теория 
вероятностей и математическая статистика) ” (3 course, 5 semester) refers to a part of the 
block of disciplines (modules) formed by participants in educational relations, and is a compul-
sory discipline. 
To study this academic discipline, the following knowledge, skills and abilities are required, 
formed by the previous disciplines: “ Discrete Mathematics (Дискретная математика)", "Calcu-
lus (Непрерывная математика)". 
The knowledge gained as a result of mastering the discipline “ Probability Theory and Math-
ematical Statistics (Теория вероятностей и математическая статистика)" are necessary for the 
successful conduct of research and development. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Formation of students' competencies in using the foundations of probability theory and 
mathematical statistics to solve professional problems.  
Tasks:  
• The study of the basic concepts and principles underlying the theory of probability and math-
ematical statistics, as well as the presentation of modern methods that are widely used in this 
science;  
• Mastering the technique of solving the main types of problems in the theory of probability; 
• Formation of students' skills in the study of mathematical models based on probabilistic 
methods.  
• Study of methods for collecting, processing and analyzing statistical data.  
 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, 
skills and abilities. 
To understand and analyze:  
• classical definition of probability,  
• addition and multiplication theorems for probabilities, 
• total probability and Bayes formulas, 
• basic concepts related to the Bernoulli scheme,  
• the concept of a random variable and its distribution function, 
• numerical characteristics of random variables, 
• Bernoulli, Poisson distributions, normal distribution,  
• the law of large numbers,  
• basic concepts of mathematical statistics, 
• classification of statistical assessments,  
• basic methods of obtaining estimates 
 
To create and to be able to: 
• find the probability of an event using the classical definition,  
• solve the main types of problems on the theorem of addition and multiplication of probabili-
ties, formulas of total probability and Bayes,  
• solve the main types of problems on the Bernoulli independent test scheme,  
• find the distribution function for discrete and continuous random variables,  
• find the numerical characteristics of discrete and continuous random variables, 
• find the main characteristics of the sample, 
• apply methods of statistical estimation. 
 
To apply:  
• applying the knowledge gained to build mathematical models,  
• using computer programs to solve problems in mathematical statistics  
 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competen-
cies: 
      General professional competences (ОПК) 
      ОПК -1. Able to apply fundamental knowledge gained in the field of mathematical and 
(or) natural sciences, and use them in professional activities 
      Indicator 
      ОПК -1.1. Applies the basic provisions and concepts in the field of mathematical sciences 
and basic terminology in solving problems of professional activity 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Random events 
Topic 1.1. Random events. Classical and geometric probability 
Random events and operations on them. The classical definition of probability. Basic proper-
ties of classical probability. Probability addition theorems for joint and inconsistent events. Ge-
ometric probability. 
Topic 1.2. Conditional probability. Total probability and Bayes formulas 
Determination of conditional probability. Independence of events. Probability multiplication 
theorems for dependent and independent events. The probability of at least one event occurring. 
Formula of total probability. Bayes' formula. 
Topic 1.3. Bernoulli independent test scheme. Markov chains 
Bernoulli independent test scheme. Bernoulli's formula. Most likely number of occurrences 
of an event in independent trials. The local Moivre -Laplace theorem and its application. The in-
tegral theorem of Moivre-Laplace and its application. Poisson's formula. Polynomial distribution. 
Markov chains. 
 
Section 2. Random variables 
Topic 2.1. Discrete and continuous random variables. Distribution function of a ran-
dom variable 
The concept of a random variable. Distribution function of a random variable and its proper-
ties. Discrete random variables. Binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, geometric distribu-
tion. Continuous random variables. Probability distribution density and its properties. Even dis-
tribution. Normal distribution and its properties. 
Topic 2.2. Numerical characteristics of random variables 
The mathematical expectation of a random variable and its probabilistic meaning. Examples 
of calculating the mathematical expectation. Mathematical expectation properties. Dispersion of 
a random variable. V ariance calculation examples. Dispersion properties. Correlation coefficient 
and its properties. 
Topic 2.3. The law of large numbers 
Chebyshev's inequality and its consequences. Chebyshev's theorem (the law of large num-
bers in the form of Chebyshev). Bernoulli and Poisson's theorems. Markov's theorem. The con-
cept of the central limit theorem. 
 
Section 3. Elements of mathematical statistics 
Topic 3.1. Selective method 
Sample. The statistical distribution of the sample. Sample mean and sample variance. Poly-
gon and histogram. Empirical distribution function. 
Topic 3.2. Statistical estimates of distribution parameters 
Statistical evaluation concept. Point and interval estimates. Point estimates classification. Meth-
od of moments for point estimation of distribution parameters. Maximum likelihood method. 
Pearson distribution. Student's distribution. Confidence Interval Method. 
 
7. Basic educational technologies 
Conducting lectures with elements of discussion, practical and laboratory studies with ele-
ments of students' creativity. The educational process is based on the concept of competence -
based learning, focused on the formation of a list of professional competencies and the practical 
application of the obtained theoretical knowledge. 
 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control: work in practical classes, homework and laboratory work. 
Midterm control: control works. 
Final certification: exam

name: Basics of Programming (Основы программирования)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course  
“Coding Theory (Теория кодирования)" 
 
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Algebra and Discrete Mathematics V .V . 
Mkrtichyan 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
 
2. Total load 
5 credits  
3. Course sequencing 
Academic discipline “ Coding Theory ( Теория кодирования)" (4rd year, 7th semester) 
refers to a part of a block of disciplines (modules) formed by participants in educational 
relations,educational program 02.03.02 "Theoretical Computer Science and Information 
Technologies" and is an optional discipline.

Section 2. Decoding methods.

name: Database Technology (Технологии баз данных)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
Database Technology (Технологии баз данных) 
Compiled by: Associate Professor of the Department of Applied Mathematics and Programming 
Cherdyntseva M.I. 
1. Program title, degree, study mode 
Direction of training: 02.03.02 Theoretical Computer Science and Information Technologies 
(Фундаментальная информатика и информационные технологии) 
Graduate qualification (degree): Bachelor 
Full-time form of education 
2. Total load 
5 credit points (180 hours), of which 36 hours of lectures, 54 hours of laboratory studies, 90 hours 
of independent work 
3. Course sequencing 
The academic discipline "Database Technology (Технологии баз данных)" (3rd year, 5th semester) 
refers to a part of the block of disciplines (modules) formed by participants in educational relations, and 
is a compulsory discipline. 
To study the discipline " Database Technology ( Технологии баз данных)" the student needs 
knowledge, skills and abilities formed by the previous disciplines " Basics of Programming ( Основы 
программирования)", "Programming Languages (Языки программирования)". 
The knowledge and skills gained in the course of studying this discipline can be used to solve 
professional problems in research, scientific production and design activities, in particular, when 
developing programs as part of graduation qualification works. 
4. Course aims and objectives 
Study of modern methods and technologies for the development of relational databases. Mastering 
the skills of using databases, writing queries in the SQL language, programming stored procedures and 
triggers, administering and managing transactions in distributed systems. 
Tasks:  
studying the basics of the relational database model, learning the SQL query language; 
mastering the technologies for developing a database schema, the principles of normalizing 
relations, mechanisms of restrictions in database schemas; 
study of programming techniques on the side of the database server, familiarization with the 
capabilities of stored procedures and triggers; 
studying the basic techniques of database administration and transaction management in multiuser 
systems. 
5. Intended learning outcomes 
As a result of mastering the discipline, the student must have the following knowledge, skills and 
abilities: 
To understand and analyze:  
• the advantages of storing information in databases; 
• capabilities of modern database servers; 
• the basics of the SQL language for accessing information in a relational database;  
• basic principles of organization of relational databases; 
• principles of transaction management in multi-user systems; 
• the role of stored procedures and triggers in databases; 
• basic tasks and tools for database administration; 
• the basic principles of organizing the interaction of applications on Java and databases 
To create and to be able to: 
• use databases in solving various professional problems; 
• develop SQL queries using table joins, grouping and subqueries;  
• use stored procedures for server-side programming; 
• use triggers to implement restrictions, correct information and log user actions; 
• use database administration tools to manage users, archive / restore the database, analyze 
performance and optimize performance. 
To apply:  
• use modern DBMS and SQL query language in solving practical problems. 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at the formation of the following competencies: 
 General professional competences (ОПК) 
 ОПК-2. Able to apply computer / supercomputer methods, modern software, including those of domestic 
origin, to solve problems of professional activity 
 Indicator 
 ОПК-2.3. Uses modern software to solve professional tasks 
 
6. Course content 
Section 1. Basics of relational databases. SQL language 
Topic 1.1. Information systems  needs. DBMS functions. Typical DBMS organization. General 
concepts of the relational approach to database organization. Basic tools for manipulating relational data. 
Problems and disadvantages of organizing file-based information systems. The concept of metadata. The 
principle of joint storage of information and metadata. Database management systems functions. Data models, 
relational model. Basic manipulation tools in the relational model. Relational completeness and relational closure 
Topic 1.2. SQL language. Functions and main features. SQL standardization 
SQL language - data description statements, data manipulation statements, transaction control statements, 
rights management statements. SQL standard and dialects. Implementation of relational operations by means of 
the select statement. Subqueries and rela tional closure. Views and their role in the development of information 
systems. Operations for entering, editing and deleting data. Firebird Server SQL language - main features and 
modern extensions. 
Section 2. Procedural extension of the SQL language. Server side programming 
Topic 2.1. Purpose of stored procedures. Syntax of SQL procedural extensions for describing stored 
procedures. 
Stored procedures (functions) - server side programming tool. SQL standard requirements and modern 
stored procedure implementations. Structural operators. Inclusion of SQL statements in stored procedures, name 
conflict issue. Cursors, syntax and implementa tion features of operations with cursors, cursor loops, scrolling 
cursors. Stored procedures in Firebird DBMS, procedures returning tables. 
Topic 2.2. Triggers. Purpose of triggers. Syntax for describing triggers. 
The goals of introducing triggers. The difference between triggers and stored procedures. Table triggers 
- trigger execution phase, the concept of a modified row. Tasks solved using triggers. Session triggers. 
Topic 2.3. Examples of practical application of procedures and triggers  
Types of information systems tasks that require server -side programming. Examples of solving such 
problems using stored procedures and triggers. 
Section 3. Database schema design. Information systems development 
Topic 3.1. Relational database design using decomposition, normal forms, normalization 
Problems with poorly designed relationships (tables). Classification of relationships based on functional 
dependencies between attributes. Identifying potential keys. Normal forms NF1, NF2, NF3, BKNF. The 
relationship between NF3 and BKNF. Normalization of  tables using a lossless decomposition algorithm. 
Examples of using the decomposition algorithm. 
Topic 3.2. Semantic data modeling, ER diagrams. Tools to support the design of databases and 
information systems. 
Entity-relationship diagrams as a means of semantic modeling of the subject area. Rules for building 
relationships based on ER diagrams. Database schema modeling applications (case tools). Simplification 
techniques in the modeling process - the introduction of surrogate primary keys, denormalization, replacement of 
reference tables, restrictions. Database schema design examples are typical cases. Tools for describing the 
database schema in SQL. Features of data types in the database. The concept of constraints in the database schema, 
means of implementing constraints. Primary and foreign key constraints. 
Topic 3.3. Organization of access to the database from applications in high-level languages. 
Features of the development of applications on the Java, organizing access to the database. Embedded 
SQL, Usage Issues, Purpose of Introducing Dynamic SQL. Organization of access through the application API. 
Application level interface standardization, acc ess drivers. Java language and access via JDBC drivers. Object -
relational approach, Hibernate technology. 
Section 4. Transaction Management. Database administration. 
Topic 4.1. Transactions and Database Integrity. Transaction management. Transaction isolation 
levels. Locking mechanism and multi-version database organization. 
Database transactions. Committing and rolling back a transaction. Transaction log. Transaction conflicts. 
Problems arising from various conflicts. ACID requirement for concurrently executing transactions. Transaction 
isolation levels. Transaction isolation  tools - locks, timestamps, data versions. Isolation levels in Firebird. The 
model of the operation of transactions in the system with data versions, mechanisms for managing obsolete 
versions. 
Topic 4.2. Database administration tools. Access rights management. Archiving and restoring a 
database 
Purpose and capabilities of administration utilities. Database administration tasks. Security issue, user and 
role management. Issuance and revocation of rights. Maintenance of the database, making copies. Tasks to be 
solved when performing archiving / restoring. Administration tools in Firebird DBMS. 
Topic 4.3. Indexing, query execution plans. Organization of the storage structure. Optimization of 
the database server. 
Query execution plan, plan optimization by the database server. Indexes, clustered and non -clustered 
indexes, the impact of indexes on query execution plans, index selectivity. Query execution plan management. 
Organization of the database storage structure , improving performance by sharding. Storage structure analysis 
tools for Firebird DBMS. 
Questions for self-study 
ADO.NET Data Provider technology for accessing a database from an application for the .NET platform. 
New features of modern DBMS. Comparison of Firebird and PostgeSQL servers. 
7. Basic educational technologies 
When conducting lectures and laboratory classes, the following educational technologies are used: 
• multimedia lectures; 
• electronic forms of control; 
• self-testing of students. 
The educational process is based on the concept of competence-based learning, focused on the formation 
of a specific list of professional competencies, updating the theoretical knowledge obtained. The deployment of 
a competency-based learning model involves the widespread use of innovative ways of organizing the educational 
process, including the use of a project-based learning method, technologies of guided self-study, including a point-
rating system, as well as the introduction of an online support system for students' out-of-class work. 
8. Formative and Interim assessment methods  
Current control: attending lectures, performing laboratory work. 
Mid-term control: testing, control works, performance of individual tasks. 
final examination: credit, set according to the results of work in the semester.

name: Physical Culture and Sport (Физическая культура и спорт)
text:
ANNOTATION of the course 
Physical Culture and Sport (Физическая культура и спорт) 
 
1. Areas of training: all areas of bachelor’s and specialist’s degrees. 
2. Total labor intensity 2 z.e., 72 hours. 
3. Place of discipline in the structure of the educational program  
The discipline program was developed taking into account modern 
interdisciplinary scientific research in the field of formation, preservation and 
strengthening of human health on the basis of integration humanitarian processes 
in educational systems for physical education. 
The academic discipline “Physical Culture and Sport (Физическая культура и 
спорт)” belongs to the Block “Disciplines (Modules)” of educational programs in 
accordance with the Federal State Educational Standard for Higher Education.  
2.2. To study this academic discipline, one need a basic level of knowledge, skills 
and abilities acquired in the process of previous secondary (complete) general 
education in biology, chemistry, and physical education: 
Knowledge: 
- anatomical and physiological characteristics of the structure and functioning of 
the human body; 
- the influence of health-improving systems of physical education on health 
promotion, prevention of diseases and bad habits.  
Skills: 
- identify the main factors influencing health; 
- create a set of physical exercises. 
Skills: 
- control of physical activity for health purposes; 
- implementation of individually selected complexes of health -improving physical 
culture. 
4. The purpose and objectives of studying the discipline  
The purpose of the discipline: the formation of a meaningful and responsible 
attitude towards one’s health through modern scientific knowledge about health 
and healthy functioning, innovative physical education and health technologies, 
health-preserving behavior skills that ensure full-fledged social and professional 
activities. 
Objectives of the discipline: 
- to create a need for self-development through the formation of personal physical 
culture; 
- to form an understanding of the essence of a culture of health and healthy life;  
- to create motivation to maintain health as the highest value, as a necessary 
condition for personal and professional development; 
- to cultivate the need for health-improving practice to master the values of 
physical culture, their active creative use to achieve life and professional goals;  
- to develop the ability to independently develop individual health programs aimed 
at prevention, correction of weak links in one’s own health, maintenance and 
development of the body’s existing resources. 
5. Requirements for the results of mastering the discipline 
The study of this discipline is associated with the modern concept of health and a 
comprehensive health improvement strategy based on the increasing social value 
of human health. 
The process of studying the discipline is aimed at developing elements of the 
following competencies in accordance with the Federal State Educational 
Standard: 
UK-7 Able to maintain the proper level of physical fitness to ensure full-fledged 
social and professional activities: 
UK-7.1. Determines the personal level of formation of physical development and 
physical fitness indicators: 
Knows: 
- indicators of development of physical qualities; 
- indicators of the level of the functional state of the body;  
- psychological and motivational indicators used for testing those involved in 
physical culture and sports. 
Can: 
- monitor and self-monitor health status during various activities, including

UK-7.2. Uses the basics of physical education to make an informed choice of

activity: 
Knows:

- use educational, health and educational technologies in physical culture and 
sports. 
UK.7.3. Forms and uses sets of physical exercises, taking into account their impact 
on functional and motor capabilities, adaptive resources of the body and health 
promotion:
